companies.name: Sprout.ai
companies.description: Sprout.ai is an AI-powered insurance claims automation platform (InsurTech) that eliminates manual work in claims processing — automating routine claim decisions while equipping handlers with smart tooling. Its layer combines document intelligence (extracting and structuring data from claims documents, reports and photos), policy validation against coverage terms, fraud and anomaly detection, and end-to-end claims resolution across Health, Life & Disability, Motor & Auto, Home & Property, and Commercial lines of business. Sprout.ai sells to insurers and enterprise partners rather than through a self-service developer program, so there is no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures the company's identity and its published security, privacy, and compliance posture.

companies.name: CipherTrust
companies.description: CipherTrust Manager is Thales's centralized key- and data-security management platform and the control plane of the CipherTrust Data Security Platform (CDSP). It provides a unified plane for encryption key lifecycle management, secrets management, certificates, tokenization, data discovery, and policy enforcement across on-premises, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments including AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, with HSM/KMIP integration, Kubernetes and DevSecOps support, role-based access controls, and post-quantum cryptography readiness. Developers and platform teams automate it through a REST API (base path /api/v1, JWT bearer authentication), an official HashiCorp Terraform provider (ThalesGroup/ciphertrust), an Ansible collection, and PowerShell orchestration modules, plus Application Protection SDKs for embedding encryption, key management, and tokenization in apps.

companies.name: OwnBackup
companies.description: OwnBackup (Own Company) is a SaaS data protection platform providing backup, recovery, and sandbox seeding for Salesforce and other cloud applications.

companies.name: Shift Technology
companies.description: Shift Technology is a Paris-founded InsurTech company delivering AI-native decisioning and automation for the global insurance industry. Its purpose-built AI agents automate core insurance workflows — claims coverage and liability, fraud and risk detection, subrogation, injury evaluation, payment integrity, and process orchestration — for property & casualty and health insurers. Shift serves 120+ insurers across 30+ countries, including 100% of the top five U.S. P&C carriers, and has analyzed more than four billion policies, claims, and documents covering 350M+ policyholders. The company also operates the Insurance Data Network (IDN). Shift is a General Catalyst portfolio company; it markets an enterprise, contact-sales product and does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs.

companies.name: Bearer
companies.description: Bearer is a developer-first static application security testing (SAST) platform whose open-source CLI (written in Go, Elastic License 2.0) scans source code and analyzes data flows to discover, filter, and prioritize security and privacy risks. It detects OWASP Top 10 and CWE Top 25 vulnerabilities, tracks sensitive data (PII/PHI) across a codebase, and produces GDPR / DPIA / PIA privacy reports. Bearer supports Go, Python, PHP, JavaScript, TypeScript, Ruby, and Java, and integrates into CI/CD via SARIF, GitLab SAST, and reviewdog output formats. The company's commercial platform was acquired by Cycode in 2024; the Bearer CLI remains open source. Bearer surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Partech and Point Nine and has been enriched from its public docs, GitHub org, and live domain probes.

companies.name: Distroless
companies.description: Distroless images by Google contain only the application and its runtime dependencies, stripping out package managers, shells, and other OS-level utilities to minimize attack surface and image size. The smallest variant (gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12) is roughly 2 MB. Distroless ships base images for static binaries, glibc-based binaries, C/C++, Java (17, 21, 25), Node.js (22, 24), and Python 3, with multi-architecture support including amd64, arm64, arm, s390x, ppc64le, and riscv64. Adopters include Kubernetes, Knative, Tekton, and Teleport.

companies.name: Echo
companies.description: Echo is a software supply-chain security company that delivers vulnerability-free (CVE-free), secure-by-design base container images, language libraries, hardened virtual machines, serverless runtimes, and OS packages. Its artifacts are built as drop-in replacements so engineering teams eliminate known CVEs across their software supply chain without changing application code, cutting remediation toil and easing compliance with frameworks like FedRAMP, FIPS, PCI DSS, DORA, and the EU Cyber Resilience Act. Echo operates as a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) and publishes a Trust Center with SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and FIPS 140-3 assurance. The company is backed by GGV Capital.

companies.name: Knox Systems
companies.description: Knox Systems is a federal cloud compliance and managed-security company that provides an accelerated path to FedRAMP authorization for SaaS and AI vendors selling into the U.S. government, marketed as "FedRAMP in 90 days for 90% less." Its platform combines a pre-authorized FedRAMP boundary, a deployable Landing Zone, hardened images, and Knox AI — a continuous-monitoring and automated remediation engine trained on federal audit data — running across AWS, Azure, and GCP at FedRAMP Moderate, FedRAMP High, and DISA Impact Level 4. Vendors inherit Knox's authorization and controls rather than pursuing an independent ATO, and Knox reports 15+ authorizations to operate across federal and DoD agencies including DHS, FEMA, the Marine Corps, Treasury, and the VA. Knox Systems is a private company backed by Felicis, and operates a partner-led business rather than a public developer API program — as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: Seezo
companies.description: Seezo is an automated, AI-powered security design review platform. It analyzes design documents and product requirement docs (PRDs) to generate explainable, consistent, and contextual security requirements — threat models, data-flow diagrams, and component maps — before developers begin coding, then routes those requirements into the tools engineering teams already use (Jira, GitHub, Slack, Confluence, Linear, ServiceNow, and more). Seezo is SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certified. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or an OpenAPI definition; its OAuth surface authenticates users of the Seezo web app.

companies.name: Ambient.ai
companies.description: Ambient.ai (legal entity Ambient AI, Inc.) is an AI-powered enterprise physical security platform founded in 2016 by Stanford AI researchers Shikhar Shrestha and Vikesh Khanna, and headquartered in Redwood City, California. The company created the category of "Agentic Physical Security," where purpose-built computer vision and a Vision-Language Model (Ambient Pulsar) autonomously observe, detect, assess, and respond to real-world threats in real time. Ambient.ai transforms an organization's existing cameras, sensors, and access control systems into a unified intelligence layer through products including Ambient Foundation (real-time situational awareness), Ambient Advanced Forensics (investigation acceleration), Ambient Access Intelligence (PACS correlation to eliminate false alarms), and Ambient Threat Detection (150+ validated threat signatures). It integrates with 200+ ONVIF cameras and VMS/PACS platforms such as Axis, Hanwha, Avigilon, Genetec, Milestone, LenelS2, and Honeywell. The platform is SOC 2 Type II certified and GDPR/CCPA aligned, uses no facial recognition, and stores no PII. Ambient.ai is backed by a16z and Allegion.

companies.name: Arbor Networks
companies.description: Arbor Networks is the DDoS protection and network-visibility division of NETSCOUT (Arbor Networks was acquired by NETSCOUT in 2015). Drawing on more than 25 years of experience and visibility into roughly 800 Tbps of global internet traffic across 550+ service-provider and enterprise customers, Arbor builds products that detect and mitigate distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks and provide network traffic analytics. Its portfolio includes Arbor Sightline (formerly Peakflow SP) for service-provider-scale monitoring, analytics and mitigation orchestration; Arbor Edge Defense (AED) as an inline stateless perimeter appliance; the Arbor Threat Mitigation System (TMS); Arbor Cloud managed scrubbing (16 global scrubbing centers, 15+ Tbps); and Arbor Spectrum/Insight for advanced threat analytics. Arbor exposes programmatic control primarily through the Sightline "SP REST API" (a JSON:API-compliant interface rooted at /api/sp/ on the appliance) and the Edge Defense Manager (EDM) API, with first-party client tooling published on GitHub and PyPI.

companies.name: August
companies.description: August (August Home) makes Wi-Fi smart locks, keypads, doorbell cameras, and the August Connect bridge for keyless, app-controlled home entry. Founded in San Francisco and originally backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Uncork Capital, August was acquired by Assa Abloy and its product line is now unified with Yale Home; the two brands share the August mobile app. August does not publish a public device-control API for consumers — third-party integrations rely on community-reverse-engineered endpoints or aggregators such as Seam, and Yale/August partners use the developer.august.com portal. Its august.com storefront (hosted on Shopify) does, however, expose an agent-native commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp and a hosted shopping MCP server at /api/ucp/mcp for buy-for-me agents, alongside Shopify customer-account OpenID Connect discovery.

companies.name: Noble
companies.description: Noble (operated by Benga Inc.) is a no-code risk and credit decisioning platform that provides risk infrastructure for the full customer lifecycle. Fintech companies, lenders, and banks use Noble to verify customer identity, aggregate and assess credit and financial-health data from multiple sources, build and launch automated underwriting and decisioning workflows with a no-code Workflow Builder, and monitor customer behavior and creditworthiness over time. Noble exposes this capability as a SaaS platform, an API, and an embeddable widget, plus pre-built data-partner integrations, so teams can build, launch, and scale digital financial products faster. Founded in 2021 and based in San Mateo, California, Noble is a Y Combinator company backed by Insight Partners, Paradigm, and Polychain.

companies.name: Operant

Its platform delivers automatic API discovery and catalogs, API-to-API microsegmentation, protocol-specific authentication/authorization, traffic rate limiting, inline auto-redaction of sensitive/PII data, and OWASP/MITRE guardrails that block a majority of the OWASP Top 10 threats. Product lines include Agent Protector, Endpoint Protector, AI Gatekeeper, an MCP Gateway, and Cloud Application Detection and Response (CADR). Operant is SOC 2 Type II compliant and publishes open-source tooling such as Woodpecker (red teaming for AI and cloud).

It pairs automated investigation with integrated, SIEM-cost-free log management (unlimited retention with customer S3 buckets) and one-click response actions. The product is delivered as a hosted SaaS console; its public surface is product documentation and inbound connectors rather than a developer-facing REST API.

The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. It exposes no public developer API; its primary technical surface is the Game Warden platform documentation, a compliance Trust Center, and a broad certification posture (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001, CMMC, FIPS 140).

The platform pairs the voter-facing mobile app with an administrative dashboard for election officials and supports accessibility features for voters with disabilities. Voatz has run elections across seven countries for more than five million voters, with pilots and deployments for U.S. counties (West Virginia, Utah County, Denver), political parties, and international election authorities. companies.name: Otterize
companies.description: Otterize is an open-source, Kubernetes-native platform for intent-based access control (IBAC). It ships three open-source operators (intents operator, credentials operator, network mapper) deployed via Helm, a Go CLI, and a managed Otterize Cloud. companies.description: Carbide (carbidesecure.com) is a compliance-automation and risk-management platform that pairs software with credentialed security advisors to help fast-growing organizations achieve and maintain security certifications and regulatory compliance. The platform automates evidence collection, maps controls across frameworks, tracks remediation tasks, surfaces compliance gaps, and continuously monitors cloud and business-tool integrations. Carbide supports SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, CMMC, CPCSC, GDPR, CCPA, NIST 800-53, NIST 800-171, PCI DSS, PIPEDA, and custom frameworks, and offers penetration testing and a customer-facing Trust Center product. Carbide is a Techstars portfolio company.

companies.name: Ordr
companies.description: Ordr provides AI-powered security for connected devices, delivering a Cyber Asset Attack Surface Management (CAASM) platform that discovers, classifies, and secures IT, IoT, OT, and IoMT devices across enterprise networks. The platform combines device intelligence, risk and vulnerability management, network segmentation, and zero-trust enforcement to move organizations from visibility to action. Ordr integrates with existing security and networking infrastructure (Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Fortinet, Aruba, Juniper) and serves healthcare, manufacturing, financial services, government, and retail sectors. The company is headquartered in Santa Clara, California. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and enriched from Ordr's public web surface; Ordr does not publish a public developer API or developer portal.

companies.name: Scytale
companies.description: Scytale is an AI-powered Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platform that automates security compliance for cloud and SaaS companies. It combines AI agents with in-house compliance experts to automate evidence collection, continuous control monitoring, cross-framework control mapping, and audit-readiness across 80+ frameworks including SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, SOX ITGC, C5, and CMMC. The platform connects to cloud providers, LLMs, HRIS, and security tooling, and offers a customizable customer-facing Trust Center plus integrated penetration testing. Scytale is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners.

companies.name: Sprinto
companies.description: Sprinto is a security and compliance automation platform supporting SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA,

companies.name: Vorlon
companies.description: Vorlon is an agentic ecosystem security platform that helps enterprises deploy AI agents and SaaS applications safely by protecting sensitive data in real time. The platform maps and monitors data flows between AI agents, enterprise applications, SaaS platforms, and cloud data stores, detecting threats, masking sensitive data in transit, and restricting agent access. Its patent-pending DataMatrix engine models the SaaS ecosystem — linking alerts, identities, APIs, data flows, and secrets — and a remote MCP server lets LLMs query security data and orchestrate investigations. Vorlon is backed by Accel and is SOC 2 Type II certified.

companies.name: Zafran Security
companies.description: Zafran Security is an AI-native threat exposure management (CTEM) platform for security teams buried in vulnerabilities and manual remediation work. It brings vulnerability findings together across an organization's existing scanners and tools to create a unified view of exposure across the hybrid enterprise, then determines actual exploitability by analyzing runtime presence, internet reachability, and existing compensating controls. Zafran maps vulnerabilities to controls the team already owns to mitigate risk before patching, and its RemOps capability uses generative AI to consolidate overlapping CVEs into a clear get-well plan routed to the right owners through existing ticketing platforms. The platform is delivered as a SaaS product accessed at api.zafran.io behind Descope-based authentication with API-key access for integrations (Axonius, Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR); it does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI. Zafran is backed by Menlo Ventures.

companies.name: Blackberry
companies.description: BlackBerry Limited is a Canadian intelligent security software and services company headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, and listed on the NYSE and TSX as BB. Once known for its smartphones, BlackBerry today builds embedded and cybersecurity software for enterprises and governments. Its portfolio spans QNX (a real-time operating system for automotive and embedded/IoT systems), Cylance AI-driven endpoint protection, BlackBerry UEM (Unified Endpoint Management), BlackBerry AtHoc critical event management and mass notification, BlackBerry SecuSUITE secure voice and messaging, BlackBerry Workspaces secure file sharing, and the BlackBerry Dynamics secure mobility platform. Developers integrate with these products through REST APIs and SDKs, including the BlackBerry UEM Web Services REST API, the BlackBerry AtHoc API (v2, REST with OpenID Connect / OAuth 2 auth), and the BlackBerry Dynamics SDKs for iOS, Android, Cordova, and React Native. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the pipeline from BlackBerry's public developer surface.

companies.name: Bridgecrew
companies.description: Bridgecrew was a developer-first cloud security company that pioneered infrastructure-as-code (IaC) security by creating Checkov, the open-source static analysis scanner for Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, Helm, ARM, Serverless, and Dockerfile configurations. Founded in 2019 and backed by Battery Ventures, Bridgecrew shipped a SaaS platform that scanned IaC and connected cloud accounts for misconfigurations, enforced policy guardrails in CI/CD, and remediated findings through automated pull requests. Palo Alto Networks acquired Bridgecrew in March 2021 for roughly $156 million and folded the platform into Prisma Cloud (now the PANW Application Security offering). The standalone Bridgecrew developer API and docs.bridgecrew.io documentation have since been retired, while Checkov remains actively maintained open source under the bridgecrewio GitHub organization and the www.checkov.io docs site.

companies.name: Didi
companies.description: DiDi Global is a mobility technology platform best known for ride-hailing, taxi-hailing, and enterprise employee travel across China and international markets. DiDi exposes a public developer surface through DiDi Enterprise Services (DDES) — an Open API for corporate travel management covering approval workflows, bills, budget/cost centers, orders, single sign-on, users, roles, and company entities. The DDES API (base URL https://api.es.xiaojukeji.com) is documented at opendocs.xiaojukeji.com/version2024, secured with OAuth 2.0 client_credentials plus per-request signing, and shipped with official Java and Go SDKs under the github.com/didi organization. DiDi is backed by Hillhouse and the SoftBank Vision Fund.

companies.name: RapidFort
companies.description: RapidFort is a software supply chain security platform focused on container hardening and automated CVE remediation. Its platform analyzes container vulnerabilities across build and runtime, profiles what software actually executes, and removes unused components to shrink the attack surface - remediating up to 95% of CVEs without code changes. RapidFort publishes a registry of 9,000+ near-zero-CVE curated container images and malware-scanned open-source libraries, and its CART capability automates compliance validation and remediation reporting for programs such as FedRAMP, cATO, CMMC, NIS2, and SOC 2. The company operates its platform through a hosted web application and a command-line workflow (analyze, profile, harden), with an open-source community-images catalog and the Kimia Kubernetes-native OCI image builder published on GitHub.

companies.name: 7AI
companies.description: 7AI (Seven AI, Inc.) is a Boston-based cybersecurity company building an agentic security platform that offloads repetitive, non-human security-operations work to swarming AI agents. Founded in 2024 by Cybereason co-founders Lior Div and Yonatan Striem-Amit, 7AI delivers "Service as Software" for the SOC: autonomous agents ingest and triage alerts, enrich data, and run end-to-end investigations, response, threat hunting, and case management so human analysts focus on high-value work. The platform spans Cases, Investigations, Detection, Response, Hunting, and Enterprise Insights. 7AI is a Greylock-backed portfolio company and raised the largest cybersecurity Series A on record. This API Evangelist profile is a company/identity record; 7AI does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: Clearvector
companies.description: ClearVector is an identity-driven detection and response platform for cloud production environments. It attributes every action in real time to human, non-human, and third-party identities across AWS, GCP, and Azure, threading together activity across GitHub, CI/CD pipelines, cloud control planes, and runtime (EC2, Lambda, containers). Per-customer predictive behavioral models surface risky behavior, and one-click isolation contains compromised identities and resources without disrupting production. Offered as SaaS, an Enterprise plan, and a ClearVector Private SaaS deployment for teams that need complete infrastructure control. Backed by Menlo Ventures. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; ClearVector publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface — the product is delivered through a login-gated application at app.clearvector.com.

companies.name: Hyground
companies.description: Hyground GmbH (Hamburg, Germany) builds a sovereign, self-hosted AI SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) agent for European enterprises. The multi-agent platform deploys as a Kubernetes-native Helm chart inside the customer's own perimeter and correlates Kubernetes, observability (Prometheus, Loki, Elasticsearch), cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), CI/CD, and ticketing data to produce evidence-backed root cause analysis, autonomous incident response, and scheduled operations work such as CVE blast-radius mapping, RBAC drift audits, cluster right-sizing, and cost triage. It runs read-only by default, is bring-your-own-model (Azure OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama), and keeps all data in-cluster with no external egress, targeting GDPR, BaFin, DORA, and NIS2 compliance requirements. Backed by partech; raised a EUR 3M pre-seed round.

companies.name: Three UK
companies.description: Three UK (Hutchison 3G UK Limited, Reading, England) is a United Kingdom mobile network operator that launched in 2003 as the country's first 3G-only carrier and grew into a consumer and business mobile, 5G, and home broadband provider, also operating the SMARTY sub-brand. Since 31 May 2025 Three UK has been a wholly owned subsidiary of VodafoneThree, the merged Vodafone UK / Three UK joint venture that is 51% Vodafone Group and 49% CK Hutchison Holdings, serving roughly 27 million UK customers. In the telecom value chain Three UK is a network owner and access provider, not a developer platform: it sells connectivity, spectrum-backed coverage, wholesale and MVNO capacity, and business connectivity, while its group-level enterprise, IoT, private-network and wholesale propositions are marketed through CK Hutchison's CKH IOD and Three Group Solutions. Its API posture is partner-gated and sales-led. Three UK publishes no public developer portal, no self-serve signup, no downloadable OpenAPI, no SDKs, and no public Postman workspace; every candidate developer hostname (developer, developers, docs, apis, sandbox, opengateway) resolves only to a wildcard Akamai record whose certificate does not cover it, and the Wayback Machine holds no snapshot of a Three UK developer portal ever existing. Three UK is nonetheless a real participant in the sector's standards layer: it is named in the CAMARA Project's governance participants list, its parent CK Hutchison Holdings is listed as an Operator in the CAMARA landscape, and on 23 September 2025 CK Hutchison Group Telecom (Three) commercially launched CAMARA KYC Age Verification and KYC Tenure network APIs alongside BT/EE, Virgin Media O2, and Vodafone under GSMA Open Gateway, on top of an already-available SIM Swap API, with KYC Match committed. Those APIs are reachable only through channel partners and aggregators — JT Group and TMT.ID are named as processing UK operator network API traffic, and Three UK's majority owner Vodafone Group is a founding venture partner in Aduna — never through a Three UK developer surface.

companies.name: Anomali
companies.description: Anomali is an enterprise cybersecurity vendor whose Agentic SOC Platform unifies threat intelligence, security data, and agentic AI. Its flagship ThreatStream is a leading Threat Intelligence Platform (TIP) that operationalizes indicators of compromise across a Unified Security Data Lake with SIEM, SOAR, and XDR capabilities. Anomali exposes a ThreatStream REST API (api.threatstream.com) for managing intelligence, observables, investigations, and integrations, and maintains a partner marketplace of prebuilt integrations. This API Evangelist profile was seeded from the general-catalyst portfolio and enriched from Anomali's public surfaces (status page, security/responsible-disclosure program, privacy and terms pages, GitHub organization, and blog).

companies.name: Clearview AI
companies.description: Clearview AI is a U.S.-based facial recognition company providing identity verification, investigative search, and biometric matching services primarily to law enforcement, government agencies, and approved financial sector customers. The platform indexes publicly available images and exposes proprietary facial recognition technology through a controlled, customer-vetted developer surface. Public technical documentation of the API is intentionally limited; access is gated, and integrations are scoped through customer agreements with strict use-case, audit, and transparency requirements.

companies.name: Cyberwrite
companies.description: Cyberwrite is an AI-powered cyber insurance intelligence platform, founded in 2017, that turns raw data into explainable, defensible financial decisions for the cyber insurance market. Its proprietary 4SEEN AI engine assesses cyber risk, forecasts breaches, simulates financial impact, and recommends mitigation, giving brokers, carriers, reinsurers, MGAs, ILS investors, and corporates access to cyber risk analytics, catastrophe modeling, and risk quantification on more than 100 million companies worldwide in seconds and in eight languages. Cyberwrite delivers its scoring and analytics through an enterprise API for real-time aggregated risk management; the platform is a Gartner Cool Vendor and DIA Top 100 InsurTech, and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company.

companies.name: Own (OwnBackup)
companies.description: Own (formerly OwnBackup, now Own from Salesforce) is a SaaS data protection platform that provides backup, recovery, archiving, sandbox seeding, and data security and compliance for cloud applications including Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, and ServiceNow. Founded in 2015 and acquired by Salesforce in 2024, Own helps organizations protect and manage the data held in their business-critical SaaS systems against loss, corruption, and compliance risk. Own is delivered as a managed product rather than a public developer API platform: it operates a public system status page and a trust center listing its security certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001/27701, FedRAMP, HDS, GDPR, HIPAA/HITECH) and a published vulnerability disclosure policy, but does not currently publish an open, self-serve REST/OpenAPI developer surface.

companies.name: Complyance
companies.description: Complyance is an AI-powered Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platform for enterprise security, risk, and compliance teams. It automates manual GRC workflows across controls management, policy management, risk management, third-party and vendor risk management (TPRM), and customer trust, using purpose-built AI agents for evidence review, control advice, policy drafting, and vendor questionnaire and risk scoring. Complyance ships 100+ ready-made frameworks (including SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, NIST CSF 2.0, CMMC, and GDPR) plus 100+ enterprise integrations to centralize evidence and support audits at scale.

companies.name: CardinalOps
companies.description: CardinalOps is a cybersecurity company delivering agentic detection engineering for security operations centers (SOCs). Its Threat Coverage Optimization Platform continuously assesses detection posture across SIEM and EDR tools (Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Cortex, Elastic and others), maps existing detections to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, surfaces coverage gaps, and automatically remediates broken or noisy rules. The Agentic Fleet and Cardinal AI use large language models to extract atomic TTPs from threat intelligence and generate new, validated detection rules. CardinalOps is backed by Battery Ventures and serves enterprise SOC teams. It publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public developer-adjacent, security, and compliance surface.

companies.name: Mimic
companies.description: Mimic is an enterprise cybersecurity company building ransomware and AI-threat defense based on "Known-Good Enforcement" at the kernel level. Its SaaS platform models a system's authorized state and blocks unauthorized modifications, detecting ransomware in fractions of a second to deflect attacks before they can encrypt data or damage infrastructure, and providing rapid-recovery technology that restores in seconds-to-minutes rather than days. Product lines include Ransomware Defense, AI Shield (Guard/Patch/Trace) and Agentic AI Governance. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, Mimic raised a $27M seed and a $50M Series A led by GV (Google Ventures) and Menlo Ventures, with Ballistic Ventures, Team8, Wing Venture Capital and Shield Capital participating; former Mandiant CEO Kevin Mandia joined its board. The platform is enterprise/government-facing (sold via demo, no public developer API) and is aligned with GDPR, SOC 1 & 2, IL4/IL5 and holds FedRAMP Ready status. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead.

companies.name: Pynt
companies.description: Pynt is an API security testing platform that helps developers identify and remediate security vulnerabilities in REST APIs including CSRF, Injection attacks, and insecure direct object references.

companies.name: Trustdock
companies.description: TRUSTDOCK Inc. (株式会社TRUSTDOCK) is a Tokyo-based digital identity and eKYC (electronic Know Your Customer) provider founded in November 2017. The company delivers high-precision, fast, and low-cost online identity verification and digital ID infrastructure via API, serving more than 300 enterprise and government clients across finance, insurance, ride-sharing and car-sharing, telecommunications (MNO/MVNO), real-estate crowdfunding, second-hand/reuse goods, recruitment, matching apps, and public-sector onboarding. TRUSTDOCK offers both browser-based and mobile-app-based verification flows, holds ISMS (ISO 27001) certification and the Japanese PrivacyMark, and participates in the OpenID Foundation Japan KYC Working Group and the FIDO Alliance. Its API documentation is provided to customers under NDA rather than published to a public developer portal.

companies.name: Exaforce
companies.description: Exaforce is a security operations platform that pairs AI agents with a unified data layer to help teams detect, triage, investigate, and respond to threats faster. Its four autonomous "Exabot" agents (Detect, Triage, Investigate, and Respond) automate SOC workflows across 100+ data sources spanning cloud, identity, endpoint, SaaS, and code repositories, and can run as a self-operated platform or as a managed detection and response (MDR) service staffed by expert analysts working alongside the AI 24/7. Exaforce positions itself as an agentic-SOC alternative to traditional SIEM tooling while retaining integration compatibility. The company is backed by Mayfield and profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API or reference documentation is currently published; this profile captures the company's public web, security, and trust surface.

companies.name: Habu
companies.description: Habu was a data clean room and data collaboration company, founded in 2017 and headquartered in San Francisco, that let brands, publishers, and media platforms run privacy-safe joins and analytics on each other's first-party data without moving or exposing raw records. In January 2024 Habu was acquired by LiveRamp, and the product now ships as LiveRamp Clean Room within the LiveRamp data collaboration network. The standalone habu.com domain now 301-redirects to liveramp.com, and Habu's former developer surface (docs.habu.com, developer.habu.com) no longer resolves — the successor developer, security, and compliance surfaces live under liveramp.com. This profile originated as a portfolio-lead stub (backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Wing Venture Capital) and is enriched here to reflect the acquisition and the real, still-live security posture inherited by LiveRamp.

companies.name: Sourcepoint
companies.description: Sourcepoint is a New York City-headquartered enterprise privacy and consent management technology company founded in 2015 by Ben Barokas and Brian Kane. The platform began as an ad-block recovery solution for publishers and evolved into a Consent Management Platform (CMP) used by leading global publishers and brands — including Axel Springer, Bauer Media, CNN International, Future, Haymarket, LADBible, Autotrader, and Ancestry — to handle GDPR, CCPA, U.S. Multi-State Privacy (USNAT), LGPD, and other regulations under the IAB TCF v2.2 and IAB Global Privacy Platform (GPP) frameworks. Sourcepoint products include the multi-campaign CMP across web, AMP, mobile (iOS, Android, React Native), Unity, Roku, HTML5 OTT and CTV surfaces, Compliance Monitoring (Diagnose), DSAR Handling, Universal Consent & Preferences, Marketing Preferences, Privacy Lens, and tooling for ad-block recovery. The Sourcepoint Public API exposes REST endpoints for GDPR TCF, GDPR Standard, U.S. Multi-State Privacy, Global Enterprise consent, and Preferences history, plus reporting endpoints for dashboards. Sourcepoint technology powers over 30 billion consumer touchpoints per month. In July 2025, Sourcepoint was acquired by Paris-based Didomi (a Marlin Equity Partners portfolio company) to consolidate global consent management; Sourcepoint continues to operate under its existing brand and developer surface during integration.

companies.name: Agari
companies.description: Agari is an email-security provider that pioneered and helped author the DMARC email-authentication standard to protect organizations from phishing, business email compromise (BEC), email spoofing, and brand impersonation. Founded in 2009, Agari was acquired by HelpSystems (now Fortra) in May 2021 and is delivered as Fortra's email-security portfolio, including DMARC Protection / Brand Protection, Phishing Defense, and Phishing Response. The Agari Platform exposes a RESTful JSON API secured with OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials for retrieving security telemetry, auditing users and domains, tracking DMARC policy enforcement, and integrating Agari data into SIEM and SOAR tooling. It was originally backed by Norwest Venture Partners and other venture investors before its acquisition.

companies.name: CACI International
companies.description: CACI International provides information technology, professional services, and managed solutions to U.S. federal government agencies in the defense, intelligence, homeland security, and civilian markets. The company delivers expertise and technology across C3I, cyber, digital solutions, enterprise IT, mission support, space, and spectrum superiority domains.

companies.name: Sazabi
companies.description: Sazabi is an AI-native observability platform that helps engineering teams find and fix production issues faster. Autonomous agents watch application logs (stdout/stderr) to detect anomalies, unfamiliar errors, traffic spikes, and failed deployments without traditional dashboards, then deliver contextual, root-cause alerts into Slack and Microsoft Teams. Engineers investigate in natural language by mentioning the Sazabi agent, and the platform can hand off context to coding agents such as Claude, Cursor, and Codex or open pull requests to remediate. Sazabi instruments 35+ hosting providers with no code changes and exposes a hosted Sazabi MCP server so agents can query logs, inspect issues and projects, and discover Sazabi tools. Founded by Sherwood Callaway; part of the Y Combinator P26 (Spring 2026) batch; backed by an $8M seed round led by J2 Ventures, Village Global, and Y Combinator, with an open beta.

companies.name: Strongkeep
companies.description: StrongKeep is a cybersecurity platform built for small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) that lack a dedicated IT team or a large security budget. It bundles malware protection, scam and phishing protection, security-awareness ("secure habits") training, human-risk monitoring, and compliance readiness (such as Cyber Essentials) into a single dashboard, with most customers reportedly going live within 60 minutes. StrongKeep offers a free no-install security scan, plans starting at $39/month, and vertical solutions for healthcare clinics and professional-services firms. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global. StrongKeep does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from its public web surface (identity, security.txt, and domain-security probes).

companies.name: Entropy
companies.description: Entropy is a threshold-signature network for trustless, programmable key management and distributed key generation (DKG). Positioned as "the Autonomous Agent Network," Entropy lets users and agents produce cryptographic signatures without any single party ever holding the private key, using on-chain WASM "programs" that define the exact conditions under which a signature may be generated. Built as a Substrate-based blockchain with a network of Threshold Signature Scheme (TSS) servers running inside Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), Entropy delivers secure crypto custody, programmable signing, and distributed key management for Web3 and autonomous-agent use cases. Backed by a16z and surfaced into the API Evangelist network via the venture-portfolio pipeline.

companies.name: LifeSite
companies.description: LifeSite is a data protection and digital asset company that helps organizations safeguard sensitive information, simplify compliance, and digitally verify ownership. Its Vault product is an encrypted store for personally identifiable, financial, and health information used by both enterprises and families to organize and collaborate on vital documents. TokenX, its Web3 arm, tokenizes real-world assets — critical minerals, carbon credits, and sports and consumer goods — so provenance and ownership can be authenticated without blockchain expertise. A Wellness product covers health, testing, and vaccination tracking for enterprises and events, and a Platform offering exposes LifeSite's building blocks and APIs for partners building tailored data-management applications. LifeSite is sales-led: the Platform APIs are described publicly but no developer portal, API reference, or specification is published, and access is arranged through a demo request.

companies.name: Token
companies.description: Token Security is a cybersecurity company that secures non-human identities (NHIs) and AI agents across on-premises, hybrid, and cloud environments. Its platform continuously discovers every AI agent, service account, and machine identity, maps ownership and security posture, detects identity threats, and automates remediation. Capabilities span NHI inventory, security posture management, lifecycle management, secrets, and identity threat detection and response. The company also ships the Token MCP Server and a native Token AI Agent so security teams can query and act on NHI data conversationally from Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Cursor. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, GGV Capital, and Qiming, Token Security serves enterprise security teams, CISOs, and IAM professionals governing machine and agent identity at scale.

companies.name: Warblerlabs
companies.description: Warbler Labs is a San Francisco fintech and blockchain company (founded 2020 by Blake West and Michael Sall) that builds and contributes to the Goldfinch Protocol, a decentralized credit protocol for real-world asset lending that provides stablecoin loans and yield generated by off-chain economic activity, and UID (Unique Identity), a KYC/KYB-compliant on-chain identity NFT. The public developer surface is the Goldfinch smart-contract system on Ethereum, an open-source monorepo (github.com/goldfinch-eng), a hosted GraphQL subgraph that indexes protocol state, and developer documentation at dev.goldfinch.finance. Security is central: every release is audited by external firms (CertiK, Trail of Bits) and the protocol runs a $500k Immunefi bug bounty.

companies.name: Array US
companies.description: Array US (Array) is a New York-based embedded finance and fintech infrastructure company. Array provides white-label, embeddable consumer credit, identity, and financial data products that banks, credit unions, fintechs, and consumer brands integrate into their own apps and marketing funnels through Array's developer tools, embeddable components, and APIs. Its product catalog includes credit score monitoring (My Credit Manager), identity and privacy protection, credit building (BuildCredit account and rent reporting), background checks, debt management and navigation, subscription management, property and home-value data, financial calculators, student loan aid, and a personalized Offers Engine and marketplace. Array is backed by Battery Ventures among other venture investors and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company.

companies.name: Crogl
companies.description: Crogl is an enterprise AI security operations platform that deploys autonomous AI agents to investigate security alerts and threat advisories entirely within a customer's own infrastructure. Using a neurosymbolic approach that combines knowledge graphs, large language models, and security best practices, Crogl gathers context, queries existing security tools, and cross-references data across SIEM, EDR, ticketing, and data-lake systems without exfiltrating data. It is tool-agnostic — integrating with Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, CrowdStrike, ServiceNow, Jira, Databricks, Snowflake, Amazon S3, and Cribl — and every action is auditable so human analysts retain final decisions. Crogl is offered as a free single-user deployment and an enterprise plan with SSO, RBAC, and 24/7 SLAs. It is a Menlo Ventures portfolio company. Crogl does not currently publish a public REST API, OpenAPI specification, or developer SDK; its API surface (connectors) is part of the on-premises product.

companies.name: Orchid Labs
companies.description: Orchid Labs is the company behind Orchid, an open-source, decentralized marketplace for bandwidth and a privacy-focused VPN. Orchid lets users pay for VPN service through nanopayments settled on a probabilistic payment layer built on Ethereum, using the OXT utility token and Orchid Accounts rather than traditional subscriptions. The stack includes an open-source multi-hop VPN client (Dart), the Orchid DApp for account creation and management, a decentralized directory of bandwidth providers running as smart contracts, and an L2/L3 nanopayment protocol. Backed by a16z, Sequoia Capital, DFJ, and Polychain, Orchid Labs focuses on decentralized privacy infrastructure rather than a conventional developer REST API.

companies.name: Sym
companies.description: Sym was a developer-first authorization and access-management platform for platform, security, and infrastructure engineering teams. Rather than a REST API, Sym exposes its control plane as infrastructure-as-code: teams declare access flows, environments, targets, and user-facing fields with the Sym Terraform provider, customize runtime behavior with the Python SDK (hooks and reducers in impl.py), and operate the platform with the symflow CLI. It automated context-based, time-bound access requests and approvals across AWS (IAM, SSO), Okta, GCP, Jira, Slack, and other targets with centralized governance embedded in an organization's existing SDLC. The Sym product is now largely wound down — the docs root is sunset and most source repositories under github.com/symopsio are archived — but its published packages, Terraform provider, and changelog remain available.

companies.name: Appriss Retail
companies.description: Appriss Retail provides AI-powered solutions that help retailers manage Total Retail Loss across in-store and online channels. Its SaaS platform combines data intelligence, decision intelligence, and workflow intelligence to reduce returns fraud, shrink, and exceptions in real time. Marquee products include Appriss Engage (return and claims authorization, incorporating the Verify return-authorization engine), Appriss Secure (shrink and exception analytics), Appriss Incident (case management), Sidekick (an AI collaborator for loss-prevention teams), and the APIS performance-intelligence platform. Appriss Retail serves more than 60 of the top 100 U.S. retailers, drawing on 20+ years of retail data science. Programmatic integration is delivered to retailer clients through the APIS Online cloud portal rather than a public self-serve developer program.

companies.name: Ensighten
companies.description: Ensighten is an enterprise tag management, data governance, and client-side website security platform. It gives digital, marketing, and privacy teams centralized control over the third-party tags, scripts, and vendor code that run on their web and mobile properties, enforcing consent and privacy rules (GDPR, CCPA) at the point of data collection. The platform combines server- and client-side tag management, malicious-script and data-leakage detection (client-side security), and consent management. Ensighten was acquired by CHEQ (CHEQ AI Technologies Ltd.) and is now delivered as part of CHEQ's Control & Compliance / Go-to-Market Security suite; the ensighten.com domain 301-redirects to cheq.ai. This company profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline. Ensighten publishes no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; it is a hosted SaaS console (manage.ensighten.com) with a Zendesk-based help center, so most spec-derived artifacts are not applicable.

companies.name: Kount
companies.description: Kount is a Boise, Idaho-based fraud prevention and chargeback management platform, now operating as part of Equifax. Kount combines AI-driven risk scoring, device fingerprinting, identity intelligence, and a multi-tenant global data network to help merchants, payment processors, and digital businesses stop payment fraud, account takeover, and chargebacks while reducing false positives. The Kount 360 platform offers Payments Fraud, Account Takeover Protection, Chargeback Management, and Identity Trust services exposed through REST APIs, mobile SDKs, a JavaScript Data Collector, and e-commerce platform plugins.

companies.name: Native Security
companies.description: Native Security is a cloud security control plane that unifies security posture and enforcement across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and OCI. The platform translates security intent expressed in natural language into enforceable architectural controls, shifting teams from reactive detection toward proactive, secure-by-design defense using built-in cloud security primitives. Capabilities include multi-cloud policy enforcement from a single definition, automated organization topology discovery and mapping, architectural segmentation and perimeter enforcement, AI-agent guardrails through architectural boundaries, and compliance automation with audit readiness. Native Security is backed by General Catalyst. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; product documentation and the application console sit behind authentication.

companies.name: BT Group
companies.description: BT Group plc (British Telecommunications) is the United Kingdom's largest fixed-line, broadband, and mobile communications provider, headquartered in London with operations spanning consumer, business, wholesale, and global enterprise markets. The group is organised around three customer-facing brands — BT, EE, and Plusnet — and a wholesale division that sells capacity and access to other communications providers. BT Group operates the UK's largest mobile network (EE), runs fibre and copper access through Openreach (a legally separate group company), and provides networked IT and security services to multinational enterprises and the UK public sector. The group publishes a public developer programme at developer.bt.com that exposes a growing catalogue of REST APIs across two main domains: charging and crediting (Direct Carrier Billing, Crediting, Premium SMS) and digital identity / fraud prevention (SIM Swap, Network Identity, Call Divert Protection), alongside wholesale and operational APIs (Broadband One, Quote Management, Address Management, Appointment Management, Product and Network Availability, HubCo Voice, Global Voice Services, IMEI Lookup, Home Network, Rail Insights, Location Insights for London, and a Travel Journey API Platform). The portal supports sandbox onboarding with Client ID / Client Secret OAuth 2.0 credentials and progression to production under a commercial agreement with an account team. In April 2025 BT announced a federated API management partnership with Kong (Kong Konnect) to consolidate its previously fragmented API estate, strengthen governance, and offer a self-service developer experience across the group.

companies.name: DeepIP
companies.description: DeepIP is an AI-powered patent intelligence platform that streamlines the full patent lifecycle for intellectual-property professionals, automating repetitive work while keeping a human in the loop. It supports invention capture, patentability assessment, patent drafting and drawings generation, AI review, prosecution support, freedom-to-operate (FTO) and invalidity searches, portfolio and landscape intelligence, and agentic prior-art search. DeepIP embeds directly into Microsoft Word, IP management systems, and the web browser, and works across chemistry, biology, software, mechanical, and electronic domains and multiple patent jurisdictions (USPTO, EPO, PCT, UKIPO, CNIPA, KIPO, and others). The company operates a zero-data-retention policy on U.S.-based Microsoft Azure and holds SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, and GDPR compliance. DeepIP is backed by Balderton Capital.

Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Chennai, India, M2P operates across 30+ countries and processes 20+ billion transactions for 50+ million end customers. Its modular, cloud-native, API-first product suite lets businesses embed financial services — core banking (Turing CBS), card issuance (credit, debit, prepaid, forex), UPI, cross-border payments, loan origination and management (Finflux), merchant management, BNPL, microfinance, KYC (Syntizen), reconciliation (Recon360), fraud and AML monitoring, 3DS access control, and neobanking — with up to 5X faster go-to-market.

companies.name: Pindrop Security
companies.description: Pindrop is an Atlanta-based voice security and identity company founded in 2011 by Georgia Tech researchers. Its "Real Human + Right Human" platform detects deepfakes, prevents fraud, and authenticates callers across voice, video, and digital channels for contact centers and virtual meetings. Core products are Pindrop Pulse (deepfake and synthetic-voice detection), Pindrop Protect (near real-time fraud risk assessment), and Pindrop Passport (multifactor voice, device, and behavioral authentication, including VeriCall technology). Pindrop holds 300+ patents and integrates with contact-center and meeting platforms such as Amazon Connect, Genesys, Five9, NICE, Cisco Webex, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams. The company is an enterprise, sales-led vendor and does not publish a self-serve public developer portal or open API.

companies.name: Rockstar Games
companies.description: Rockstar Games is an American video game publisher headquartered in New York City and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Take-Two Interactive Software (NASDAQ: TTWO). Rockstar does not publish a public developer portal; its HTTP API surface is internal and consumed only by first-party clients (game executables, the Rockstar Games Launcher, and Rockstar's mobile companion apps). The most visible public-facing API is its OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 identity provider at signin.rockstargames.com, which exposes standard /connect/authorize, /connect/Token, /connect/introspect, and /.well-known/jwks endpoints. Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled to launch on November 19, 2026 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S and will include a "significant online mode" succeeding GTA Online.

companies.name: Anjuna

Its Seaglass platform, Policy Manager, Overwatch agentic-AI governance, and Northstar AI data clean room deliver hardware-rooted cryptographic attestation and policy-based access control for sensitive workloads and privacy-preserving AI. Anjuna is delivered as command-line runtime tooling and open-source attestation libraries rather than a public HTTP API.

companies.name: Fhenix
companies.description: Fhenix is a blockchain R&D company building confidential computing for EVM-compatible chains using Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE). Its CoFHE (FHE Coprocessor) lets Solidity smart contracts compute directly on encrypted data — encrypt inputs client-side, operate on ciphertexts on-chain via the FHE.sol Solidity libraries, and unseal results through a threshold decryption network, so sensitive state stays private without ever being decrypted on-chain. The developer stack is a smart-contract-plus-client-library surface (not a REST API): the cofhejs TypeScript SDK, Hardhat/Foundry plugins and starters, the fhenix-contracts Solidity libraries, and mock contracts for local testing. CoFHE is live on public testnets (Ethereum Sepolia, Arbitrum Sepolia, Base Sepolia) with mainnet planned. Fhenix is backed by Multicoin Capital.

companies.name: Cyence
companies.description: Cyence is a cyber risk analytics and modeling solution — originally an independent InsurTech startup (backed by IVP and others) and acquired by Guidewire in 2017 — that helps insurers, reinsurers, brokers, and managing general agents quantify, underwrite, and manage cyber insurance risk in financial terms. It combines internet-scale data collection, data science, and economic loss modeling to produce exposure signals, breach-probability estimates, and portfolio accumulation and catastrophe scenarios. Cyence data and scores are delivered to carriers through Guidewire Cloud and are available via a REST API for pricing, risk selection, and underwriting workflow automation. API access is partner-gated through a Guidewire account rather than a public self-serve developer portal.

companies.name: Dropsuite
companies.description: Dropsuite, now a NinjaOne company, is a cloud backup, archiving, and recovery platform built for managed service providers (MSPs) and their small-to-midsize business customers. It provides automated backup and one-click restore for Microsoft 365, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, email, and website/database data, plus long-term email archiving with legal hold, eDiscovery, and journaling for compliance. Partners manage tenants through a multi-tenant portal and can automate provisioning, reporting, and reconciliation through a partner REST API gated to Direct Partners and Distributors (credentials issued in the Partner Portal under Settings -> API Settings). Dropsuite was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Intego
companies.description: Intego is a consumer cybersecurity company with more than 25 years of Mac and Windows protection, headquartered in France (Intego S.A.). Its flagship Intego ONE suite bundles antivirus with real-time threat detection, a network firewall, the SmartClean disk-cleanup and performance optimizer, and Intego VPN for encrypted private browsing, sold as separate macOS and Windows product lines. Intego also runs The Mac Security Blog, a long-running source of Apple and macOS security reporting. The company publishes a Compliance Hub for procurement and vendor-security reviews and holds an active ISO/IEC 27001:2022 information-security certification. Intego is a consumer software vendor and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile was surfaced as a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio lead and enriched with its public identity, security, and compliance surface.

companies.name: Zama
companies.description: Zama is an open-source cryptography company building state-of-the-art Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) solutions for blockchain and AI. Its developer surface is a suite of libraries and protocols rather than a hosted REST API: TFHE-rs (a Rust implementation of TFHE), Concrete (a Python-to-FHE compiler), Concrete ML (privacy-preserving machine learning), fhEVM and the Zama Protocol for building confidential smart contracts and dApps on EVM-compatible chains, plus TypeScript SDKs (the fhEVM Relayer SDK and React SDK). Zama publishes the ERC-7984 confidential token standard, a developer hub, GitBook documentation, and an active open-source GitHub organization. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and enriched from Zama's public developer surface.

companies.name: Flashpoint
companies.description: Flashpoint is a threat intelligence company delivering decisive intelligence for cybersecurity, fraud prevention, corporate and physical security, vulnerability management, insider threat, and national security teams. Its Ignite platform and Flashpoint API surface data collected from illicit online communities, the deep and dark web, chat services, and open sources — exposing threat actors, compromised credentials, vulnerabilities, and fraud indicators. Flashpoint makes this finished intelligence and raw data available programmatically through a REST API at api.flashpoint.io, documented at docs.flashpoint.io, so security teams can integrate alerting, data feeds, and finished intelligence into SOC, SIEM, and security automation workflows.

companies.name: Humio
companies.description: Humio is a log management and observability platform built for ingesting, storing, and searching machine data in real time at scale. Backed by Accel and acquired by CrowdStrike in 2021, Humio is now delivered as CrowdStrike Falcon LogScale. It provides high-throughput streaming ingest (including Splunk HEC and Elastic bulk compatible endpoints), a live query language for dashboards and alerts, and index-free retention. Developers integrate through a REST API for ingest and search plus a GraphQL API for administration (repositories, parsers, users, ingest tokens), with official client libraries for Python, Node.js, Go, and JavaScript and the humioctl command-line client.

companies.name: Singtel
companies.description: Singtel (Singapore Telecommunications Limited) is Singapore's largest mobile network operator and the anchor communications group of Southeast Asia, with a regional footprint that includes Optus in Australia and associate stakes in Airtel, AIS, Globe and Telkomsel. In the network-API value chain Singtel sits on the supply side: it owns the mobile network signals — SIM, line, device, location, call state — that the CAMARA specifications turn into callable APIs, and it packages them for Singapore as SingVerify, a five-API anti-fraud and identity suite built on the GSMA Open Gateway framework. It also operates Paragon, its own 5G/edge/network orchestration platform, which powers the Bridge Alliance API Exchange (BAEx) federating network APIs across Bridge Alliance member operators, and it is one of the twelve carrier equity partners in Aduna, the Ericsson-led joint venture that aggregates operator network APIs into a single global commercial channel. Its API posture, however, is partner-gated and sales-led: as of July 2026 there is no first-party developer portal (developer., developers., docs. and opengateway. subdomains do not resolve), no published OpenAPI, no sandbox, no SDKs and no self-serve signup. Every SingVerify and CPaaS API page on singtel.com terminates in an enterprise enquiry form, and the BAEx portal is an explicit login wall for approved partners. Developers reach Singtel's network capabilities through aggregators — Aduna and its platform partners (Vonage, Sinch, Infobip, Google Cloud), the Bridge Alliance exchange, or identity vendors such as IPification — rather than directly from Singtel. Two surfaces do exist and are captured here: www.singtel.com publishes a first-party llms.txt family (root plus consumer, support and corporate companion files, last updated 2026-06-30) that indexes its marketing and support estate for AI systems while naming none of its APIs, and Singtel runs a footer-linked vulnerability disclosure programme at vdp.singtel.com and on HackerOne. api.singtel.com is a live Apigee gateway behind Imperva that answers every unrouted path with an Apigee fault envelope — a real gateway with nothing publicly bound to it.

companies.name: Chui
companies.description: Chui, now operating as Trueface (part of BigBear.ai after the Pangiam acquisition), is a facial recognition and computer vision company. Originally launched as "Chui," the world's first faceprint API for access and identity, the technology is delivered today as a licensed developer SDK with C++, Python, Android, and iOS bindings, plus a Dockerized on-premises REST API (Trueface On-Prem / PTOP) for 1:1 and 1:N face matching, spoof and liveness detection, object detection, and identity verification. Deployment options span on-device, self-hosted Docker, and AWS. The technology has been evaluated in NIST FRVT and DHS/CBP testing and is applied across fintech, education, security, healthcare, retail, hospitality, and government. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled by the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: EigenDA
companies.description: EigenDA is a secure, high-throughput, decentralized data availability (DA) service built on top of Ethereum using EigenLayer restaking primitives. Developed by Eigen Labs and operated as the flagship product of EigenCloud, EigenDA accepts blobs of rollup data from rollup sequencers, erasure-codes them, distributes the chunks across a network of EigenLayer-restaked operators, and produces aggregate BLS signatures that anchor data availability on Ethereum L1. The service is positioned as a hyperscale DA layer for rollups, advertising 1 GB/s of design throughput and is secured by 4M+ ETH restaked through EigenLayer with validators that include Coinbase, Google, Nethermind, and Puffer. EigenDA is consumed today by rollups and chains including Celo, MegaETH, and Aevo, with integrations available for Arbitrum Orbit, OP Stack, Nitro, and the Sovereign SDK. The protocol exposes a gRPC API surface across a Disperser (blob ingest and status), Relays (blob and chunk retrieval), Retriever (reconstructive retrieval), Churner (operator registration), and Validator/Node endpoints. v2 of the protocol introduces a payment vault and the GetPaymentState RPC on the Disperser, replacing per-account static throughput reservations with a programmatic payments surface. The reference implementation is open source in Go (with a Rust client and SDKs in Rust and TypeScript), licensed Apache-2.0 / MIT, and developed in the open on GitHub.

Aceiss installs from the GitHub Marketplace as a read-only app requiring admin privileges and exposes an API for integrating its real-time access data into existing systems, with spreadsheet and PDF export. It integrates with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace via API in about five minutes with no MX record changes, can run in monitoring mode, provides explainable incident response with Indicators of Compromise for CISOs, and reduces false positives by up to 90%. Founded by former Google Safe Browsing, reCAPTCHA, and Web Risk leaders Cy Khormaee (CEO) and Ryan Luo (CTO), AegisAI raised a $13M seed round co-led by Accel and Foundation Capital in 2025 and is SOC 2 Type II certified.

Additional products include the Brink's Armored Account payment processing service, Brink's Money paycard for employee payments, and RetailBox point-of-sale cash management.

companies.description: Deduce is a New York City-based identity intelligence and fraud-prevention company focused on detecting stolen and synthetic identities, including the rapidly growing class of AI-generated identities used to bypass traditional Know Your Customer and onboarding controls. The company operates the Deduce Identity Graph, an activity-backed U.S. identity network the firm describes as covering 185 million weekly active users and 1.5 billion daily events, used to deliver real-time multi-contextual risk and fraud signals during new account opening, login, and checkout. Deduce sells a real-time API-based fraud-risk scoring product, a Multicontextual Identity Insights service, and a browser-based dashboard for traffic segmentation, anomaly detection, and forensic review, with pre-built integrations into common identity platforms (Auth0, Microsoft Entra External ID / Azure AD B2C, ForgeRock / Ping, Gluu) alongside a native REST API. The company sells to banks, fintechs, lenders, BNPL providers, retail, travel, and payments platforms; its commercial model is enterprise contracts, and its developer documentation, OpenAPI definitions, and integration guides sit behind an authenticated portal, with no public GitHub repositories, no public SDKs, and no published machine-readable API specification.

companies.name: Securiti
companies.description: Securiti is a San Jose, California data security, privacy, and AI governance company that markets the Data Command Center, a unified hybrid multicloud platform for sensitive data discovery, classification, security posture management, privacy operations, and AI governance. The platform is built on the Data Command Graph, a knowledge-graph layer that correlates data assets, identities, regulations, and AI systems across 1,000+ pre-built connectors spanning AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Snowflake, Databricks, and major SaaS applications. Securiti's product surface includes Data Security Posture Management (DSPM), Sensitive Data Intelligence, Data Access Intelligence, Data Flow Governance, Data Minimization, Breach Impact Analysis, Data Subject Request (DSR) Automation, Universal Consent Management, Mobile App Consent SDKs, Assessment Automation, Data Mapping, Privacy Center, the People Data Graph, Data Catalog, Data Lineage, Data Quality, Compliance Management, AI Security and Governance, Agent Commander for AI risk detection, Security for AI Agents and Copilots, and the Gencore AI suite for safe enterprise AI copilots, vector-database synchronization, unstructured data curation, and context-aware LLM firewalls. The platform exposes REST-based APIs, a turnkey JavaScript consent library, standards-based webhook interfaces, no-code/low-code workflow integrations, and native mobile SDKs for iOS and Android consent capture. The API reference, SDKs, consent banner generators, and connector catalog are all reached through the Securiti app and Privacy Center; full API documentation requires an authenticated tenant. Securiti was founded in 2018 by Rehan Jalil and has been recognized as a Gartner Customers' Choice and an IDC Worldwide Leader in data privacy and data security. The company's revenue model is enterprise SaaS subscription with usage-based connector and module pricing; no public free tier or self-serve API key issuance is currently offered.

companies.name: Signal Sciences
companies.description: Signal Sciences is a web application and API protection (WAAP) company whose Next-Gen Web Application Firewall (WAF) and Runtime Application Self-Protection (RASP) defend web apps, APIs, and microservices against the OWASP Top 10, account takeover, and malicious bots without the tuning burden of legacy WAFs. Founded in 2014 by Andrew Peterson, Nick Galbreath, and Zane Lackey and backed by CRV, Index Ventures, and others, Signal Sciences was acquired by Fastly in October 2020 for approximately $775M and is now sold as the Fastly Next-Gen WAF. The product retains its own control plane and REST API at dashboard.signalsciences.net/api/v0, which remains live for existing customers and lets developers programmatically manage corps, sites, requests, events, custom signals, rules, redactions, lists, rate-limited sources, thresholds, virtual patches, and workspace alerts. Product documentation now lives on the Fastly developer documentation site.

companies.name: DataGrail
companies.description: DataGrail is a San Francisco-based data privacy platform founded in 2018 by Daniel Barber and Ignacio Zendejas that helps enterprises automate privacy operations and manage regulatory compliance risk across GDPR, CCPA, and other global privacy regimes. The platform combines a Live Data Map for real-time visibility into where personal data lives across an organization's SaaS and cloud footprint, a Request Manager for orchestrating Data Subject Requests (access, deletion, opt-out) across thousands of downstream systems, a Consent solution for cookie and tracker compliance with automated enforcement, a Risk Management module for privacy and AI risk assessments (PIA, DPIA, AI risk), and an embedded agentic AI named Vera that surfaces context-aware recommendations across the platform. DataGrail exposes a documented public REST API at /api/v2 covering authentication, assessments, privacy requests, opt-out requests, integrations, webhooks, integration files, and consent audit logs, alongside an open-source ecosystem on GitHub that includes mobile Consent SDKs for iOS and Android, a Google Tag Manager consent template, and a Terraform AWS ECS module for deploying Request Manager Agents. The company serves enterprise customers including Salesforce, HubSpot, Okta, Netgear, and Dexcom, advertises 2,000+ pre-built integrations across CRM, marketing, communications, HR, data, e-commerce, and support platforms, holds patents on its Live Data Map and Smart Verification technology, is SOC 2 and ISO certified, and is backed by Felicis Ventures, HubSpot Ventures, Okta Ventures, Basis Set Ventures, Cloud Apps Capital, Operator Collective, Thomson Reuters Ventures, and Third Point Ventures.

companies.name: Odaseva
companies.description: Odaseva is an enterprise data security, backup, and governance platform purpose-built for large, complex Salesforce environments. It provides data backup and recovery, archiving, seeding and anonymization/masking, encryption and key management, privacy and data-residency controls, and data governance for regulated enterprises. Odaseva holds SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001:2022, HITRUST, HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA, TISAX, IRAP, MLPS 2.0, and CSA STAR Level 2, with independent audits by Ernst & Young. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network; Odaseva sells to enterprises and does not publish a public developer API portal, OpenAPI, or SDKs at this time.

companies.name: Quantcast
companies.description: Quantcast is a San Francisco-headquartered digital advertising and audience intelligence company founded in 2006. Its flagship offering is the Quantcast Platform, an AI-driven demand-side platform (DSP) for programmatic display, video, CTV, audio, mobile, and native advertising, powered by the company's proprietary Audience Graph and Ara AI engine. Quantcast also operates Quantcast Measure, a free audience measurement product that has tagged millions of digital properties to produce demographic, psychographic, and cross-device audience insights. For programmatic access, Quantcast exposes a developer portal at developers.quantcast.com built around a GraphQL API (v2) for reporting, campaign management, and audience operations on the Quantcast Platform, secured via OAuth 2.0 client credentials. A server-to-server Conversion API augments the browser-side Live Tag for offline and signal-loss-resilient conversion tracking. Quantcast Choice, the company's IAB TCF v2-compliant Consent Management Platform, was acquired by InMobi in August 2023 and is now operated as part of InMobi CMP; legacy Quantcast Choice mobile SDKs remain published under the quantcast GitHub organization for reference. Quantcast also open-sources the Quantcast File System (QFS), a C++ distributed file system, and mobile/Roku measurement SDKs.

companies.name: Upstream Security
companies.description: Upstream Security is a cloud-based automotive and smart-mobility cybersecurity company. Its purpose-built vehicle data platform delivers Cyber XDR detection and response for connected vehicles, runtime AI and API security, proactive quality detection, and advanced analytics, alongside AutoThreat PRO threat intelligence and Vehicle Security Operations Center (vSOC) services for OEMs, Tier 1 and 2 suppliers, fleets, insurers, EV charging, and mobility IoT operators. Upstream publishes no public developer portal or API; the platform is sold as enterprise SaaS with demo-based onboarding.

companies.name: SentinelOne
companies.description: SentinelOne is an AI-driven extended detection and response (XDR) cloud security platform delivering autonomous endpoint protection, EDR, identity security, cloud workload protection, and threat hunting through its Singularity Platform. The Management API exposes the same operations as the web console for agents, threats, alerts, sites, accounts, exclusions, and policy management. Authentication uses tenant-issued API tokens passed in the Authorization header as `ApiToken <token>`.

companies.name: Blocks
companies.description: Blocks is a cloud cost-optimization service that guarantees up to 20% savings on AWS spend by aggregating the purchasing power of hundreds of companies into group-buying negotiations, then layering automated cloud management on top. Its AI-powered DevOps agent, Major Tom, continuously monitors connected AWS accounts through read-only billing access, surfaces cost-saving and security findings in Slack, and can propose Terraform fixes without requiring root or code access. Onboarding is a one-click read-only AWS cost-data integration with no long-term contracts and no infrastructure changes. Blocks is backed by Speedinvest and is profiled in the API Evangelist network; it currently exposes a marketing and product surface rather than a public developer API.

Products include Covatic Sense for individual-level connected TV (CTV) addressability and attribution, a next-generation audience DMP for enrichment, clean-room data sharing, retargeting and attribution, plus audio, podcast, and smart-speaker targeting. Covatic integrates via the Covatic Tag (no-code tag manager), the Covatic SDK (on-device processing), and a server-to-server Covatic API, with a Google Ad Manager publishing path and client data stored in EU, AU, or US regions to meet local requirements.

companies.name: Skopenow
companies.description: Skopenow is an open-source intelligence (OSINT) platform built to modernize digital investigations. Founded in 2015 and backed by Techstars, it fuses public records, consumer data, crime data, news, and online content with AI-powered fraud and threat-detection models to generate intelligence reports on entities, uncover and visualize networks between people and organizations, and surface operational risks. Its product suite spans Grid, Pre-Check, Workbench, Link Analysis, and Rabbit, serving global security, insurance, government, law enforcement, legal, and media teams — more than 1,500 organizations, including a fifth of the Fortune 500. Skopenow ships as a login-gated web application rather than a public developer API.

companies.name: Zorus
companies.description: Zorus is a cybersecurity company that provides DNS web protection and filtering built for managed service providers (MSPs), managed security service providers (MSSPs), and IT teams. Its Archon agent delivers DNS filtering without requiring per-router DNS changes, layered with CyberSight behavioral user analytics, geo-IP and network filtering, zero-trust device isolation, and SaaS inventory and usage visibility. Zorus is delivered as a multi-tenant SaaS platform administered through a partner portal (portal.zorustech.com), positioned as an alternative to Cisco Umbrella, WebRoot DNS, and WebTitan. Zorus does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation; its API surface (api.zorustech.com) sits behind the authenticated product portal. This profile captures the company's public web properties and probed security posture.

Behavox is backed by Index Ventures and the SoftBank Vision Fund.
