companies.name: Blindmate
companies.description: Blindmate is a friend-based dating app that inverts the swipe model: instead of writing their own profile, a single person's friends answer questions about them, and matches are made through character-first "Blindchats" that surface compatibility before appearance. Founded in Germany and available on iOS and Android in German, English, and Spanish, the app reports over one million users and positions itself around trust, reduced harassment, data privacy, and green-energy infrastructure. Blindmate is a Speedinvest portfolio company; it is a consumer mobile product and publishes no public developer API, so this profile captures its web, security, and policy surface rather than API artifacts.

companies.name: CloudLock
companies.description: CloudLock is a cloud-native Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) that protects data, users, and applications across SaaS, IaaS, PaaS, and IDaaS environments. Founded in 2011 and acquired by Cisco in 2016, it is now delivered as Cisco Cloudlock within Cisco Umbrella / Cisco Security Cloud. The platform uses an API-driven model to discover sensitive content, detect policy violations, flag anomalous user behavior, and manage cloud application (OAuth) risk. Developers integrate through the Cisco Cloudlock API (v2), a Bearer-token REST API exposing activities, incidents, incident entities, incident aggregates, policies, apps, entities, IP libraries, and anomalies. Originally a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, CloudLock's developer surface is documented on Cisco DevNet and the Cisco Umbrella documentation hub.

companies.name: Spirl
companies.description: Spirl is a non-human identity and access management (IAM) startup that in 2025 rebranded to Defakto (defakto.security); spirl.com now redirects to the Defakto site. The company secures automated systems — workloads, services, CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes, and AI agents — by replacing static secrets and hardcoded credentials with short-lived, cryptographically verifiable identities built on open workload-identity standards (SPIFFE/SPIRE style). Co-founded by Eli Nesterov (ex-ByteDance infrastructure) and Danny Oliveri, it targets the enterprise gap where organizations run millions of non-human identities protected only by static secrets. Defakto was named a 2025 Gartner Cool Vendor in Identity-First Security. It is a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing site, blog, and security page but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, CLI, or developer portal — access is via demo request, so there is no API surface to enrich at this time.

companies.name: Appriss Inc.
companies.description: Appriss Inc. was a Louisville, Kentucky data and analytics holding company whose business units were broken up in 2021: Appriss Insights was sold to Equifax in a $1.825 billion deal, and Appriss Health was rebranded as the independent company Bamboo Health. The surviving Appriss Retail business (apprissretail.com) is an AI-powered retail loss-prevention platform that helps retailers combat total retail loss across in-store and online channels through returns-fraud prevention, shrink and exception analytics, and case and audit management. Its products include Appriss Engage (returns and claims management), Appriss Secure (shrink and exception analytics), Appriss Incident (case and audit management), and the Sidekick AI collaborator. Appriss Retail publishes no public developer API program — its APIS Online portal is an authenticated Asset Protection Information System (customer login), not a developer API surface.

companies.name: Brevis
companies.description: Brevis is a highly efficient ZK coprocessor and zkVM that empowers smart contracts to read from the full historical on-chain data across all supported blockchains and run customizable computations in a completely trust-free way. Developers build application circuits with the Brevis SDK (available in Go and TypeScript), implementing a Data Access Module to specify the historical blockchain data needed, an App Circuit for the computation logic, and an App Contract to receive ZK-verified or coChain-verified results on-chain. Brevis also operates ProverNet, an open marketplace for zero-knowledge proofs, and Pico, an open-source high-performance zkVM. Backed by Polychain.

companies.name: Fable
companies.description: Fable Security is an AI-powered human risk management (HRM) platform that helps security teams reduce incidents by changing employee behavior. It combines behavioral interventions (targeted nudges and AI-generated content), phishing simulations, short-form video awareness briefings, and human-risk reporting into a single platform positioned as a modern replacement for legacy security-awareness training. Fable's AI Studio, Composer, and Briefing Agent generate custom video and audio content - including deepfake and voice-fake simulations - and produce audience-targeted briefings from emerging threats in minutes. The platform reports on human risk and compliance across the workforce and integrates with an organization's identity framework, workspace, and security tooling. Fable serves healthcare, financial services, and technology customers including Sisense, SanDisk, Red Hat, PennyMac, Genesys, and Dayton Children's Hospital, and is backed by Greylock and Techstars.

companies.name: Perfios
companies.description: Perfios is a Bangalore, India-headquartered financial technology (SaaS) company providing an AI-driven operating system for banks, NBFCs, fintechs, and insurers, serving over 1,000 financial institutions globally. Its platform spans four product families: Perfios Analyse (bank statement, ITR, GST, payslip, credit-card and financial-statement analysers), Perfios Verify (KYC/KYB, video KYC, liveness detection, OCR, digital signature and onboarding via OneSDK), Perfios Lens (portfolio monitoring, PFM, credit assessment memos, due diligence), and Perfios Protect (document tamper detection, deepfake detection, and insurance fraud detection). Perfios also runs a digital public infrastructure (DPI) stack for Account Aggregator FIU/FIP roles. Its data-aggregation, decisioning, and verification capabilities are delivered to partners programmatically; public developer documentation is gated behind partner access. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners.

companies.name: Prized
companies.description: Prized is an AI-powered platform that lets non-technical operations, support, and finance teams build, deploy, and share secure internal tools without engineering. Users describe a workflow in natural language (or bring their own coding agent such as Claude Code) and Prized builds real software on company data that is pre-connected and scoped, with least-privilege database access per tool, credential isolation, outbound-traffic proxying, and an audit trail on every access. Tools deploy behind corporate authentication and connect to 20+ services including Salesforce, Postgres, Slack, Stripe, and Notion. Prized is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company founded by Hudson Griffith and Marinos Eliades, both formerly of Gander (YC F24, acquired by Archer Aviation). Added to the API Evangelist network via the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched from the company's public web surface.

companies.name: Menlo Security
companies.description: Menlo Security is a cybersecurity company that secures the enterprise browser, positioning the browser as the point of control for protecting both human users and AI agents. Its cloud-native Secure Enterprise Browser and Menlo Cloud Security Platform apply remote browser isolation to prevent zero-day phishing, ransomware, and malware from ever reaching the endpoint. The platform spans AI agent security and governance, AI Adaptive DLP (data loss prevention), file security for downloads and uploads, zero-trust remote access to private applications, and threat prevention. Menlo Security is headquartered in Mountain View, California and is backed by investors including General Catalyst, Vista Equity Partners, JPMorgan, American Express Ventures, and HSBC. Menlo does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface; administration is handled through its cloud console and a customer support portal.

companies.name: Napatech
companies.description: Napatech is a Danish provider of programmable FPGA-based SmartNICs and network-acceleration hardware used for high-speed network monitoring, cybersecurity, and telecom/5G workloads. Its Link-Capture and Link-Inline software, together with the NTAPI/NTPL developer SDK, let applications capture, filter, and process network traffic at line rate with zero packet loss. The developer surface is a C/C++ hardware SDK (NTAPI) plus the NTPL programming language rather than a web/REST API; integrations ship as open-source additions to DPDK, VPP, Open vSwitch, Scapy, and Zeek via the napatech GitHub organization. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Vodafone
companies.description: Vodafone Group plc is a UK-headquartered (Newbury, England) multinational telecommunications company and one of the world's largest mobile and fixed network operators, with operations in 15 country markets and partner-market agreements covering 40+ additional countries across Europe and Africa. The group serves 279 million mobile customers, 5 million business customers, and manages 215+ million IoT connections through its Vodafone IoT platform. Beyond mobile and broadband connectivity, Vodafone operates one of the largest IoT/M2M businesses in the industry, invests in 70+ subsea cables, and runs financial services like M-PESA (Africa) and Vodapay. Through Vodafone Business it sells connectivity, cloud, security, and managed-mobility services to enterprises, and through the GSMA Open Gateway and CAMARA initiative it exposes a growing portfolio of standardised network APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location, Match, MVNO Discovery, and more) via the Vodafone Developer Marketplace (developer.vodafone.com), which publishes 27+ commercial and CAMARA APIs across Identity, Mobile, Analytics, Boost/QoS, and Partner categories. The Marketplace exposes sandbox and live endpoints under api-sandbox.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com and api.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com, with OAuth2 (Consumer Key / Consumer Secret) authentication and Postman collections for every product. Vodafone is a premier member of the CAMARA alliance hosted at the Linux Foundation, a founding participant in the GSMA Open Gateway, and one of the principal telco operators driving network-as-an-API adoption globally.

companies.name: Certa
companies.description: Certa (operated by Opinr, Inc. d/b/a Certa) is an AI-native third-party risk management (TPRM) and compliance platform that unifies the full third-party lifecycle — onboarding, due diligence, contract management, continuous compliance monitoring, and offboarding — in a single no-code system. Founded by Jag Lamba and headquartered in Saratoga, CA, Certa serves Fortune 500 companies (Honeywell, Uber, Mars, Box, Quantcast) across 120+ countries and 17 languages. The platform covers all risk domains — operational and resilience, infosec and cyber, compliance and legal, financial and credit, reputational, geopolitical, and ESG and ethical risk — via its Studio no-code process designer, Certa Connect (130+ native integrations), and embedded AI agents. Certa was named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Third-Party Risk Management Tools. External integration is available through an enterprise external API surfaced from the platform; no public OpenAPI or developer portal is published as of this profile.

companies.name: Cowbell
companies.description: Cowbell is a Pleasanton, California-based adaptive cyber insurance provider serving small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) and the middle market with standalone cyber liability coverage, technology errors & omissions (Tech E&O), management liability, and excess cyber products. Founded in 2019, Cowbell pioneered continuous underwriting through its proprietary Cowbell Factors risk benchmarking, which scores organizations against millions of data points to surface vulnerabilities and prioritize remediation. The company pairs its policies with a closed-loop resiliency program (assess-insure-respond-improve) that includes complimentary risk assessments, Cowbell Insights threat detection, incident response planning, cybersecurity awareness training, micro-penetration testing, and vendor risk assessments, plus subscription-based managed detection and response (MDR), penetration testing, identity monitoring (IdentityAI), and Compliance-as-a-Service (COMPaaS). Cowbell operates across the United States (all 50 states plus DC), the United Kingdom, and Australia, is backed by reinsurance partners including Zurich, and offers a public developer program at developers.cowbellcyber.ai exposing REST APIs for agencies, accounts, risk factors, quoting, binding, policy management, and webhooks across its Prime 100, Prime 250, and PrimeOne products. The API surface powers digital aggregator integrations with partners such as Bold Penguin, Herald, Semsee, Sayata, Limit, iBynd, and AmWins. No public OpenAPI specification or open-source SDK is published by Cowbell.

companies.name: NewCore
companies.description: NewCore is an enterprise identity-security company building an identity platform that governs both human and AI-agent identities across the enterprise. Its three pillars are Identity Discovery (continuously discovering and mapping every identity across directories, PAM, shadow systems, and AI infrastructure), Identity Security (breach prevention through phishing-resistant authentication and device-bound sessions that cannot be stolen or replayed), and Human + AI Agent Governance (minimum-access provisioning, full lifecycle management, and support for ephemeral agentic workloads). NewCore is backed by Index Ventures. It sells to enterprises via demo request and publishes a trust center (SOC 2 Type II, CSA STAR Level 1, GDPR, CCPA) but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: Nile
companies.description: Nile is a San Jose, California enterprise networking company delivering an AI-native Secure Network as a Service (NaaS). Founded in 2018 by former Cisco executives Pankaj Patel and John Chambers (chairman), Nile replaces traditional campus and branch LAN/Wi-Fi hardware-and-license procurement with a subscription-based, outcome-guaranteed wired and wireless network stack delivered as a service. The Nile Access Service combines its purpose-built Zero Trust Fabric (switches, access points, gateways, and sensors) with cloud-based autonomous operations, the Nile Services Cloud, Nile AI, Nile Nav, and Nile Digital Twin to plan, deploy, monitor, and self-heal enterprise networks. The platform emphasizes built-in Zero Trust segmentation, continuous performance guarantees (coverage, capacity, availability), and consumption-based pricing — marketed against 60%+ breach reduction, 99%+ ticket reduction, ~3x faster change management, and ~40% TCO savings versus traditional enterprise networking. Nile does not publish a general-purpose public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or Terraform provider; its programmable surface is limited to a closed admin/portal API and outbound webhooks used for documented integrations with ServiceNow (ticket and alert webhooks), Splunk HEC, CrowdStrike, Zscaler ZIA, Microsoft Entra (SCIM), Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Global Secure Access, Palo Alto Networks, Forescout (device inventory API), SecureW2, Aruba ClearPass, VeloCloud, Graphiant, Hamina, and Ekahau. Nile is available through the AWS Marketplace as a SaaS subscription.

companies.name: Elisity
companies.description: Elisity is a San Jose-based cybersecurity company (founded 2019, backed by Insight Partners) that builds an AI-powered, identity-based microsegmentation platform for Zero Trust security. Elisity discovers, classifies, and continuously monitors every user, workload, and device, then enforces dynamic least-privilege policies to stop lateral movement, without agents, new hardware, or network changes, by leveraging the Cisco, Arista, and Juniper switches organizations already own. The platform centers on Elisity IdentityGraph (real-time asset visibility enriched from sources like Active Directory, CrowdStrike, and Armis), a Dynamic Policy Engine, lightweight Virtual Edge container software that syncs policy to existing infrastructure, and the Cloud Control Center admin portal. Its product API and Open Connector integration API are documented inside the authenticated Cloud Control Center rather than a public developer portal. Elisity is used by Fortune 500 healthcare systems, manufacturers, and pharmaceutical firms for IoMT, OT/ICS, and enterprise segmentation.

The platform focuses on understanding access intent rather than static roles, enabling enterprises to adopt AI and automation securely at scale. Oasis targets enterprise security teams through a sales-led (demo-request) motion rather than a self-service developer product, and does not publish a public API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; its product documentation is a login-gated knowledge base.

Its portfolio spans private AI infrastructure (PulseAI, deployable in under two weeks for data sovereignty), AI-powered cybersecurity (AI SOC, digital forensics and incident response, and managed AI security services), Data & AI strategy and infrastructure, and Customer Experience delivered on Salesforce. Gruve targets enterprises of roughly 5,000 to 50,000 employees and serves CXOs, IT, security, and data leaders globally. Backed by Mayfield, the company operates a public trust center (SafeBase by Drata) attesting SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and ISO/IEC 42001:2023. This is a company/provider record in the API Evangelist network; Gruve is a services and platform provider and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

companies.name: HelloVerify
companies.description: HelloVerify is India's leading background verification (BGV) and employee screening company, delivering fast, accurate, and compliant primary-source verification for employment, education, healthcare credentialing, immigration, and enterprise workforce programs. The platform has completed 20M+ verifications for 2000+ organizations across 120+ countries, offering AI-powered background checks, customer KYC with identity and liveness, vendor due diligence (Certifier), and instant messaging-based verification (HelloV). HelloVerify operates an audited information-security and compliance program (ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, ISO 9001, ISO 22301, Cyber Essentials, GDPR) and serves regulators, enterprises, SMBs, and applicants worldwide. Added to the API Evangelist network as a dcvc portfolio company; no public developer API surface is currently published.

companies.name: Pindrop
companies.description: Pindrop is a voice and audio security company providing a continuous identity verification and deepfake-detection platform for enterprises. Its technology authenticates callers and video-meeting participants, detects synthetic (AI-generated) speech and fraudulent activity, and protects contact centers, virtual meetings, and connected devices. Pindrop's products span call-center fraud detection, passive voice authentication, and liveness/deepfake defense, and are delivered largely through partner platforms (Amazon Connect, Zoom, Webex, and others) rather than a public self-service developer API. The company is backed by Felicis, GV, and IVP and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

companies.name: Qevlar AI
companies.description: Qevlar AI is an autonomous Security Operations Center (SOC) platform that investigates every security alert the way a top analyst would — without playbooks, without hallucinations, and without adding headcount. Founded in 2023 by Ahmed Achchak and Hamza Sayah and headquartered in Paris, France, the company runs a proprietary graph-based AI orchestrator (not an LLM agent) that delivers deterministic, evidence-based investigations across the full security stack. As soon as an alert fires from SIEM/EDR tools, Qevlar autonomously pulls, enriches, and analyzes internal and external data, then returns a conclusive malicious/benign verdict, a full investigation report, and recommended remediation — typically in under three minutes, closing up to 80% of tickets automatically. The SaaS platform is SOC 2 Type 2 certified, hosted in the EU (Belgium) on GCP, and connects via API to 50+ security tools (Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, CrowdStrike, Cortex, Google SecOps, and more). It is trusted by Fortune Global 500 enterprises and leading MSSPs/MDRs across Europe and the US. Backed by EQT Ventures and Partech.

companies.name: EZKL
companies.description: EZKL (by Zkonduit Inc.) is a developer-friendly engine for verifiable AI and analytics that generates zero-knowledge proofs (ZK-SNARKs, Halo2) for machine learning model inference. Given a model in ONNX format and sample input, EZKL automatically compiles a proving circuit and produces a cryptographic proof that a computation ran correctly without revealing the underlying private data or model weights. Proofs are verifiable on-chain (EVM-compatible), in the browser, or on edge devices. EZKL ships as a command-line tool, Python and JavaScript (WebAssembly) bindings, and a Rust library, and supports tree-based models, transformers, CNNs, and RNNs. Lilith is its high-performance compute cluster for cloud-scale proof generation. The codebase was audited by Trail of Bits and is developed in the open at github.com/zkonduit/ezkl.

companies.name: Raven
companies.description: Raven is a runtime security platform that protects applications from the inside, detecting and preventing malicious code execution as it happens rather than relying only on perimeter defenses. Its capabilities span Runtime Prevention (blocking exploit execution regardless of CVE availability), Runtime ADR (application-level attack detection and response with forensics), Runtime AI-Agents (discovering and monitoring AI agents in an environment), Runtime SCA (prioritizing vulnerable dependencies by actual execution), and Runtime Gatekeeper (keeping risky applications out of production). The platform is self-hosted on Kubernetes, deployed via Helm/OCI charts and a sensor operator across AWS, Azure, and GCP, and is positioned as an application-level alternative to WAF, EDR, RASP, SCA, and ASPM tools. Raven is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners.

companies.name: Threat Stack
companies.description: Threat Stack was a Boston-based cloud security company providing full-stack cloud security observability, intrusion detection, and compliance monitoring for infrastructure and applications across cloud-native workloads including virtual machines, containers, and Kubernetes. Its platform combined rules and supervised machine learning to detect threats, vulnerabilities, and attacks in real time. Threat Stack exposed a RESTful V2 API (HAWK/HMAC authenticated) and trigger-based webhook alerts, along with first-party SDKs, a Go CLI, and configuration-management modules (Chef, Ansible, Puppet, Terraform, CloudFormation, Helm). The company was acquired by F5 in 2021 and the product is now F5 Distributed Cloud App Infrastructure Protection (AIP); the original threatstack.com and api.threatstack.com domains have been decommissioned.

companies.name: Enclave
companies.description: Enclave (enclave.ai) is an AI-powered application and cloud security platform that operates as an "agentic security engineer." It continuously builds a living model of an organization's attack surface across services and cloud providers, then autonomously triages and investigates vulnerability findings against known CVEs to determine real-world exploitability and reachability. Rather than flooding teams with signature-based noise, Enclave traces data flows to confirm whether a CVE is actually reachable, surfaces cross-service exploits that traditional scanners miss, and routes prioritized remediation plans with proof to the owning teams. Founded by veterans from Stripe, Box, VMware, Salesforce, and Yelp, the company is backed by 8VC and Marc Benioff. Added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from the company's public web surface; no public developer API is currently published.

companies.name: Dune Security
companies.description: Dune Security is a cybersecurity company whose User Adaptive Risk Management platform uses AI-driven behavioral analysis to quantify and reduce user-layer cyber risk. It runs omni-channel attack simulations (email/spear phishing, smishing, vishing, deepfakes, and encrypted-app lures) tailored to each employee's role and behavior, generates a live User Risk Score from five inputs (business impact, simulations, training activity, external security integrations, and historical data), and automatically adapts micro-training and security controls in real time. The platform integrates with IAM, EDR, SEG, DLP, and HRIS systems to escalate or restrict access for high-risk users, and ships an in-house training library (Security Awareness, Compliance, and Functional-Specific Training) covering NIST 800-53, NIST CSF, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX, ISO 27001, FFIEC, GLBA, and GDPR. Dune Security is backed by Craft Ventures.

companies.name: OpenVPN
companies.description: OpenVPN is a secure networking company providing VPN and Zero Trust network access solutions for over 20,000 organizations worldwide, offering both the self-hosted Access Server and the cloud-delivered CloudConnexa managed service. The platform supports encrypted tunnels, identity-based access policies, content filtering, IDS/IPS, and domain-based traffic rules across major cloud providers. OpenVPN exposes an XML-RPC management API for Access Server and an OAuth 2.0 protected REST API for CloudConnexa.

companies.name: Wiz
companies.description: Wiz is a cloud-native application protection platform (CNAPP) that provides agentless security across AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, and containers, covering CSPM, CWPP, CIEM, vulnerability management, DSPM, and threat detection in a unified security graph. The Wiz GraphQL API exposes inventory, issues, vulnerabilities, configurations, and reporting using OAuth 2.0 client credentials authentication.

companies.name: Zomma
companies.description: Zomma (Zomma Labs) is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building AI agents that automate repetitive back-office operations for investment firms — hedge funds, asset managers, and fintech companies. Rather than integrating through traditional APIs, its computer-use agents perceive and operate existing portals, desktop applications, and PDFs the way a human would (clicking, reading, typing) to handle reconciliation, client onboarding, KYC, and investor reporting, with human approval required before any submission. Zomma also markets a developer-facing computer-use API ("plug Hermes, Claude, or your own agent into our API") that is currently waitlist / pre-general availability with no public specification, SDK, or documentation.

companies.name: Ipid
companies.description: iPiD (International Payments Identity) is a fintech providing real-time Know Your Payee (KYP) verification for cross-border and domestic payments. Its single, payment-rail-agnostic API lets banks, PSPs, and corporates validate bank account ownership and match payee names before funds move, reducing authorized push payment (APP) fraud, business email compromise losses, and failed transactions. Products include iPiD Validate (global payee / bank account verification with name-matching), iPiD Node (a scheme-compliance layer for EU Verification of Payee, UK Confirmation of Payee, FATF Recommendation 16, and US Nacha), and a Payment Agent agentic verification layer. Founded in 2021, iPiD is backed by QED Investors, Monk's Hill Ventures, Quona Capital, Jungle Ventures, Saison Capital, and others. Public API access is gated behind a sales/demo process; no machine-readable specification is published publicly.

companies.name: PDI Technologies (fka PDI Software)
companies.description: PDI Technologies (formerly PDI Software) is a global provider of software and data solutions for the convenience retail and wholesale petroleum industries, serving 200,000+ customers across 60+ countries. Its portfolio spans PDIQ (an AI foundation for convenience and fuel operations), PDI Enterprise wholesale petroleum software, ERP and back-office systems, POS and store systems, logistics, loyalty marketing, fuel and mobility payments, an offer network, insights and analytics, cybersecurity (PDI Security and Network Solutions, formerly Echosat), and the consumer app GasBuddy. PDI is backed by Insight Partners and has grown through acquisitions including P97 Networks. The company exposes no public self-serve developer/API portal; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

companies.name: CyberTalents
companies.description: CyberTalents is a global cybersecurity platform that ranks and connects security talent with employers based on real, hands-on skills. The platform automates Capture the Flag (CTF) competitions, delivers cybersecurity courses and training camps, runs technical assessments for enterprises, and provides recruitment and headhunting services to close the global cybersecurity skills gap. Backed by 500 Global, CyberTalents operates from Egypt, the UAE, and the United States and hosts one of the largest cybersecurity practice communities in the world. This API Evangelist profile tracks CyberTalents as a company; no public API or developer program was found during enrichment.

companies.name: DevAI
companies.description: DevAI (DevAI Solutions, Inc.) is a Silicon Valley enterprise IT company, founded in 2024 by Susie Wee (CEO) and Edwin Zhang, that builds agentic AI for IT operations teams. Its DevAI Network Intelligence Engine reconciles data across fragmented IT tools of record (CMDB, vCenter, NetBox and other infrastructure, network, compute, and security systems) into a single trustworthy operational view, and its Network Intelligence Agent "Neo" streamlines IT planning, incident response, patch management, and security and compliance workflows through a chat interface. DevAI reports deployment at Fortune 50 enterprises and won Best-in-Show (Automation) at the AI Networking Summit 2025. The company raised a $6M seed round led by Emergence Capital with Pear VC, Base10 Partners, and Benchstrength. No public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal has been published to date; this profile captures the company identity and the security posture of its public web surface.

companies.name: Efflux Systems
companies.description: Efflux (Efflux Systems, Inc.) is a Baltimore, Maryland cybersecurity company founded in 2014 that operates a near real-time asset intelligence and attack-surface platform. Efflux delivers fresh intelligence about the assets of organizations, networks, and services — offered as a one-time Asset Map, scheduled monitoring, or on-demand custom scanning. Its differentiator is radical transparency: rather than opaque risk scores and surface-level abstractions, Efflux records and exposes every scan it runs, every asset it discovers, and every attribution it makes, so teams can see what was found, how it was discovered, and why it matters — raw information and formatted insights side by side. Data is accessible via export, download, share, and a programmatic API. The company is backed by 500 Global, Granite Hill Capital Partners, TEDCO, and Three Tree Ventures, and is currently in early access with a public waitlist.

companies.name: Novee Security
companies.description: Novee Security (Novee) is a cybersecurity company delivering AI-driven penetration testing that finds vulnerabilities faster, validates defenses, and reduces cyber risk. Its autonomous offensive-security platform performs penetration testing at machine speed across web applications and APIs, and spans solutions including DAST, AI red teaming, manual penetration testing, bug bounty, and compliance testing. Backed by Canaan Partners, Novee is building continuous, AI-native security testing as an alternative to traditional DAST scanning and slow, periodic manual pentest cycles. The company publishes a marketing and product site, a vulnerability glossary, and a blog, but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Perimeter VRM (formerly ProcessBolt)
companies.description: Perimeter (formerly ProcessBolt) is a vendor risk management (VRM) platform built for regulated industries. It covers the full third-party risk lifecycle through six modules — Monitor (continuous vendor surveillance and alerts), Assess (automated risk assessments with a drag-and-drop template builder), Extract (AI-powered document intelligence), Verify (attack-surface validation), Share (a document management and collaboration hub), and Respond (RFP and assessment response automation). The product centralizes vendor information, scores and reports vendor risk, and supports no-code integration and API-based / CSV vendor imports across US, EU, and Australia data regions. ProcessBolt rebranded to Perimeter and now serves the platform from perimeter.net; processbolt.com redirects there. No public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDKs are published — the platform's integration APIs are exposed to customers rather than through an open developer surface.

companies.name: Red Points
companies.description: Red Points operates an AI-powered brand protection and anti-counterfeiting platform used by businesses to detect and remove counterfeits, unauthorized sellers, fake websites, social media impersonation, and digital piracy across more than 5,000 marketplaces, social networks, and app stores. Its software combines automated detection with enforcement and takedown workflows, domain monitoring, gray-market and unauthorized-seller blocking, ad-fraud detection, and revenue-recovery and litigation services. Red Points was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network; it does not expose a public developer API or documented API surface as of this enrichment pass, so this profile captures the company's public web, legal, security, and llms.txt footprint rather than API artifacts.

companies.name: Cyral
companies.description: Cyral is a data security and governance platform (founded 2018, Milpitas CA; acquired by Varonis in March 2025) that provides an agentless, stateless data-layer sidecar for monitoring and governing access to data repositories such as Snowflake, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Amazon S3, Kafka, and Oracle. Cyral was built API-first: its Control Plane exposes a REST API secured with OAuth2 client-credentials, fully automatable through the official Cyral Terraform provider (cyralinc/cyral) and supporting Terraform modules for AWS, Azure, and Okta. Following the Varonis acquisition, cyral.com now redirects to Varonis' Database Activity Monitoring product, but the first-party developer tooling remains published on the cyralinc GitHub organization and the Terraform Registry.

companies.name: Zmanda
companies.description: Zmanda is an enterprise backup and recovery software provider and the commercial steward of the open-source Amanda (Advanced Maryland Automatic Network Disk Archiver) project. Its products protect Linux, Windows and macOS systems, databases, and application data with agent-based and agentless backups that write to local disk, tape, and public-cloud object storage. The company maintains an active GitHub organization (github.com/zmanda) around the Amanda backup engine and related tooling, operates a customer-facing management portal at the Zmanda Network (network.zmanda.com), and publishes API documentation for programmatic backup and recovery management at api.zmanda.com. Zmanda was an early portfolio company of Canaan Partners.

companies.name: Twingate
companies.description: Twingate is a Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) platform that replaces legacy VPNs with software-defined perimeters, providing identity-based, least-privilege access to private resources without exposing them to the public internet. The Twingate Admin API is a GraphQL API authenticated via API key (X-API-KEY header) that enables programmatic management of remote networks, connectors, resources, users, groups, service accounts, devices, policies, and DNS filtering profiles.

companies.name: Astrix Security
companies.description: Astrix Security is a cybersecurity company providing identity security for AI agents and non-human identities (NHIs) — the API keys, OAuth apps, service accounts, SSH keys, and MCP servers that fall outside traditional human IAM. Its platform lets enterprises discover a real-time inventory of every AI agent and NHI with business and risk context, secure them by remediating excessive privileges, misconfigurations, and abnormal or malicious activity, and deploy agentic AI safely via an Agent Control Plane that provisions short-lived, tightly scoped credentials. Founded by Alon Jackson and Idan Gour and headquartered in Boston, Astrix is backed by CRV, Bessemer Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures, F2, and Anthropic. The company was acquired by Cisco and ended standalone sales of new licenses effective June 30, 2026.

companies.name: NICKL
companies.description: NICKL (Nicklpass) is a subscription management platform that bills itself as "the operating system for subscriptions." It helps organizations govern the digital tools, SaaS subscriptions, and data services their teams use by connecting identity, usage, and procurement data in one place. Capabilities include role-based governance and provisioning, usage intelligence to surface adoption and redundant spend, and coordinated procurement that aggregates demand to negotiate from real usage data. The platform integrates with Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Plaid, and applies AI models for insights and pricing optimization. NICKL participated in the Comcast NBCUniversal LIFT Labs Accelerator powered by Techstars. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing site and hosted control panel but no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK, or other machine-readable API surface.

companies.name: Picnic
companies.description: Picnic is a London-based, privacy-first photo-organization app for iOS that helps people declutter and organize their camera roll through a swipe-based, gamified experience — sorting photos into albums, comparing and removing duplicate shots, building streaks, and resurfacing "on this day" memories. All processing happens on-device, so photos never leave the user's phone: no cloud upload, no ads, and no tracking or selling of user data. Founded in 2019 and a certified B Corporation, Picnic grew to more than 1.5 million users and roughly €4M ARR before being acquired by Paris-based mobile app publisher MWM in April 2026. Picnic is a consumer mobile product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Valid.it
companies.description: Valid.it (Validit.ai) is an AI-based fraud prevention SaaS that lets enterprises, governments, and financial institutions validate users' statements remotely and in real time through a standard smartphone, laptop, or tablet camera. Its patented physio-behavioral AI combines computer vision, signal processing, and PPG bio-signal analytics to detect deepfakes, synthetic identities, and deceptive intent across onboarding, KYC/AML, insurance claim verification, security vetting, and HR screening — delivered as a standalone web-based solution or via API integration. A Techstars portfolio company; no public developer portal or API documentation is published.

companies.name: Dtex Systems
companies.description: DTEX Systems (dtex.ai) is a risk-adaptive cybersecurity company delivering an enterprise Insider Risk Management platform that unifies human, data, and AI risk through behavioral intelligence. Its InTERCEPT platform combines lightweight endpoint telemetry, user activity monitoring, and data loss prevention with privacy-by-design pseudonymization to detect insider threats and prevent data breaches early. DTEX Platform v7 adds OCSF-aligned, cloud-to-cloud connectors and autonomous "agentic defender" AI agents (Triage Guardian, Threat Hunter) that investigate incidents, while the company's i3 investigative division provides expert insider-threat research. DTEX integrates with SIEM, SOAR, EDR, IdP, and productivity tools (Splunk, CrowdStrike, Microsoft 365, Netskope, Google Workspace) rather than exposing a public developer API. Backed by Wing Venture Capital.

companies.name: IXL Learning
companies.description: IXL Learning is a K-12 personalized practice platform with 17,000+ skills across Math, Language Arts, Science, Social Studies, and Spanish, plus the IXL Real-Time Diagnostic and skill recommendations. IXL is sold primarily as a SaaS subscription to families, teachers, schools, and districts. Its integration surface is school-rostering and SSO, not a public developer API: IXL supports Clever (SSO + rostering), ClassLink (SSO + OneRoster auto-rostering), OneRoster CSV/REST, LTI, Google Classroom, and SAML SSO for district deployments. There is no public REST API portal, no published OpenAPI, and no partner developer program.

companies.name: Periphery
companies.description: Periphery is a cybersecurity company providing embedded, device-level threat management for critical industrial and defence platforms. Its lightweight, architecture-agnostic agent secures, fingerprints, and continuously monitors devices, detecting unauthorized changes and hardening what is risky even in constrained, offline, or air-gapped environments. The platform spans three products: Insights (point-in-time security evaluation with agent-based pen-testing and SBOM risk analysis), Vantage (on-prem intelligence that establishes a known-good baseline, detects change, and restores devices), and Outpost (real-time on-device threat detection and prevention for air-gapped deployments). Periphery targets regulatory compliance across NDAA, EU CRA, NIS2, UN R155, UN R156, and IEC 62443. It is a Techstars portfolio company.

companies.name: BitAccess
companies.description: Bitaccess is a Canadian blockchain company (Ottawa, founded 2013, Y Combinator) that builds the enterprise software and hardware powering Bitcoin ATM (BTM) operations and fintech businesses in more than 15 countries. Its stack includes the Bitaccess BTM operating software, the Cash API for cash-in and cash-out crypto transaction flows, and the Catena blockchain suite for publishing complex datasets to public or private blockchains via smart contracts. Bitaccess maintains an in-house HD/multisig enterprise wallet built for high-velocity applications and publishes first-party open-source client libraries under the npm @bitaccess scope and the github.com/bitaccess organization, led by the coinlib unified Node.js/TypeScript crypto-payments library. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital.

companies.name: CohnReznick
companies.description: CohnReznick is a top-25 US accounting, tax, and advisory firm formed in 2012 by the merger of J.H. Cohn LLP and Reznick Group, P.C. The firm serves clients across more than 30 industries from offices throughout the United States and four offshore subsidiaries, with its global reach extended through membership in the Nexia International network (operating in more than 128 countries). In May 2024 CohnReznick became the first US accounting firm of its scale to receive a strategic growth investment from a private equity sponsor when funds advised by Apax Partners acquired a majority stake. As part of that transaction the firm operates under an alternative-practice structure: audit and attest services are delivered by CohnReznick LLP (a licensed CPA firm) while tax and advisory services are delivered through CohnReznick Advisory LLC. Largest practice areas include Real Estate, Renewable Energy, Government Contracting, Asset Management (private equity, hedge funds, private credit, REITs), Financial Services, Healthcare, Life Sciences, Consumer & Industrial, Technology & Media, Public Sector, and Private Clients (family offices, high net worth individuals, professional sports). CohnReznick does not publish a public software developer API; this repository documents the firm's organizational profile, practice taxonomy, and linked-data context for API catalog purposes.

companies.name: Appwrite GraphQL
companies.description: Appwrite GraphQL is a powerful API layer that exposes the full Appwrite backend-as-a-service platform through a GraphQL interface, allowing developers to query and mutate any resource type including databases, storage, users, and functions. It mirrors the complete Appwrite REST API (except OAuth) with GraphQL advantages such as selection sets and query batching, enabling precise data fetching and multiple operations in a single request.

companies.name: Cobalt AI
companies.description: Cobalt AI (formerly Cobalt Robotics) is a San Francisco based physical security automation company whose Cobalt Monitoring Intelligence platform uses AI handlers to investigate security events across access control systems and video feeds, determine root cause, and trigger automated responses so security teams focus on genuine threats instead of alarm triage. Its offerings include the Cobalt Command Center remote monitoring service and an indoor autonomous security robot, with integrations spanning LenelS2, Genetec, Avigilon, Brivo, Eagle Eye Networks, Milestone, Okta, ServiceNow, Salesforce, and Slack. The company was founded in 2016, backed early by Bloomberg Beta and Sequoia, and acquired in 2024 by Dean Drako, who rebranded it to Cobalt AI.

companies.name: Runsybil
companies.description: RunSybil is an AI-native autonomous offensive security platform. Sybil — a system of AI agents — continuously penetration tests live applications and infrastructure, finding, exploiting, and validating real vulnerabilities without a human in the loop. It tests live applications black-box by default (no source code required), integrates with GitHub and GitLab to trigger targeted change testing on every code push, and validates every finding through a multi-agent pipeline before it surfaces, aiming to eliminate triage and false positives. RunSybil positions as a replacement for point-in-time penetration testing, legacy DAST/SAST scanners, and bug bounty programs, and also offers white-box testing for deeper codebase exploration. Founded in 2023 by Ari Herbert-Voss (OpenAI's first security hire) and Vlad Ionescu (Offensive Security Tech Lead at Meta), the company raised $40M led by Khosla Ventures and is trusted by security teams at Notion, Cursor, Turbopuffer, Baseten, and Thinking Machines Lab. No public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface is published at this time.

companies.name: Udacity
companies.description: Udacity is an online tech-upskilling platform offering project-based Nanodegree programs, individual courses, and enterprise workforce development across Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Agentic AI, Data Science, Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Programming, Autonomous Systems, Product Management, and DevOps. Founded by Sebastian Thrun out of the Stanford CS221 free online AI course in 2011, Udacity pioneered the Nanodegree credential and partnered with industry leaders (AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Mercedes-Benz) to co-develop curriculum. In 2024 Accenture acquired Udacity for approximately $1B and folded the platform into LearnVantage, Accenture's enterprise learning and skilling business. Udacity reports 25M+ learners globally and remains best known for its Self-Driving Car, Deep Learning, and Generative AI Nanodegrees, with hands-on projects reviewed by human mentors and career services. Udacity does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — enterprise customers integrate via Accenture LearnVantage sales channels rather than self-service APIs. Its public GitHub organization (github.com/udacity) hosts 1,100+ open-source classroom and course-content repositories (e.g. deep-learning-v2-pytorch, self-driving-car, cd13303-genai-c1-classroom) used as Nanodegree exercises, not as official platform APIs.

companies.name: Zscaler
companies.description: Zscaler is a cloud security platform delivering Zero Trust Exchange services including Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA), Zscaler Private Access (ZPA), and Zscaler Digital Experience (ZDX). Zscaler exposes REST APIs across its product suite for configuration, policy management, and reporting, authenticated via API keys, OAuth 2.0, or session-based authentication depending on the product and cloud (zsapi).

companies.name: Aella Credit
companies.description: Aella (Aella Credit) is a technology-driven microfinance bank licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), building consumer and business financial infrastructure across Africa. Its consumer app offers savings, low-interest and same-day loans, bill payments, and high-yield savings accounts, while its Fintech-as-a-Service platform exposes that infrastructure to businesses through a developer-facing API gateway. Published API capabilities include wallet-as-a- service (create and manage digital wallets with real-time balances and full ledger support), KYC/identity verification via BVN and NIN, bank-account lookup and validation, sub-accounts and pooled fund structures for platforms and marketplaces, and direct-debit recurring collections. A live Aella Merchant API is hosted at api.aellaapp.com and a merchant dashboard at merchant.aellaapp.com, though the provider does not yet publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. This profile was seeded as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Intrinsic
companies.description: Intrinsic is a unified Trust & Safety platform that gives safety teams a single API and dashboard to detect, investigate, and enforce against abuse across user- and AI-generated content, fraud, and marketplace abuse. The platform surfaces machine-learning classifiers (for example text toxicity and IP trust scoring), account graph lineage for linkage analysis, geo enrichers, and global intelligence signals through a synchronous API, and lets teams author, version, deploy, and monitor real-time anti-abuse rules from a hosted dashboard. Founded in 2022 in San Francisco by Karine Mellata and Michael Lin (previously on Trust & Safety ML and data-engineering infrastructure at Apple and Discord), Intrinsic has since rebranded to Variance (variance.co); the Intrinsic-branded developer surfaces at docs.intrinsicapi.com and api.intrinsicapi.com remain in service.

This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Manifest Law's public discovery documents; no OpenAPI specification was published at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: Imper.AI
companies.description: imper.ai is an Israeli workforce identity security company that stops AI-driven impersonation, deepfakes, voice clones, and social-engineering attacks in real time across enterprise communication channels such as Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, and Slack. Rather than scanning message content for anomalies, the platform correlates hard-to-fake signals — device telemetry, network diagnostics, and behavioral patterns — to validate identity at high-risk lifecycle events including hiring, employee enrollment, and help-desk verification. Founded by cyber-intelligence veterans and backed by Redpoint Ventures and Battery Ventures (about $34M raised), imper.ai integrates with ATS, HRIS, IdP, ITSM, PAM, IVR, and meeting platforms, and is deployed across financial, health care, and technology enterprises. This profile was seeded from Battery Ventures' portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; imper.ai currently publishes a product knowledge base rather than a public developer API program.

Mobileum sells primarily to carriers as deployed/managed enterprise software and does not publish a public developer portal or open API surface.

companies.name: Astrix
companies.description: Astrix Security is a non-human identity (NHI) and AI agent security platform. It gives enterprises a real-time inventory of every AI agent, MCP server, service account, OAuth app, API key, SSH key and IAM role across their environment, then detects excessive privileges, misconfigurations, anomalous activity and policy violations and drives automated remediation. Its Agent Control Plane provisions secure-by-design AI agents with short-lived, precisely scoped credentials. Astrix became part of Cisco in 2026 and ended standalone sales of new licenses effective June 30, 2026. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures. Sector: cybersecurity. This is a company profile — Astrix publishes no public developer API, so the profile carries identity, security-posture, and compliance signals rather than API specifications.

companies.name: Bedrock Data
companies.description: Bedrock Data (Bedrock Labs, Inc.) is a data security posture management (DSPM) company that helps organizations discover, classify, and control sensitive data across cloud, SaaS, and on-premises environments. Its platform is built on a unified Metadata Lake that combines data sensitivity, lineage, identity and access entitlements, and data-flow analysis, layered with AI-driven classification and a natural-language policy engine, and a zero-data-access architecture in which analysis runs where the data already resides. Bedrock advertises a Graph API (GraphQL) and MCP integration surface for downstream security tooling such as SIEM, Wiz, Sysdig, and Jira, though no public developer documentation or OpenAPI is currently available. The company is backed by Greylock.

companies.name: Menlo Security
companies.description: Menlo Security provides a cloud-delivered Browser Security Platform that protects enterprises and their AI agents at the browser session layer, where most modern attacks and data loss occur. Its core capabilities include pre-render threat prevention using multimodal visual and DOM analysis, patented Positive Selection file security that reconstructs documents to strip malware and macros, AI Adaptive DLP for real-time detection and masking of PII/PHI and financial data, invisible browser isolation for high-risk activity, and Menlo Secure Application Access for identity-based zero-trust access to SaaS, legacy, and private applications for both human users and autonomous agents. The platform integrates with existing SASE/SSE, EDR/EPP, and SOC tooling through a single unified control plane. Menlo Security is privately held and backed by investors including General Catalyst. The company operates primarily as an enterprise security vendor and does not publish a public developer API program; administrative and reporting APIs are available to customers through the authenticated admin console.

companies.name: Netskope
companies.description: Netskope is a security service edge (SSE) and SASE platform delivering cloud-native Secure Web Gateway, CASB, Zero Trust Network Access, data loss prevention, and threat protection from its NewEdge global network. The Netskope REST API v2 provides tenant-level programmatic access to events, alerts, incidents, policies, IoCs, SCIM provisioning, and configuration so SOC and platform teams can automate SOAR, SIEM, and IGA workflows using service-account bearer tokens in the Netskope-Api-Token header.

companies.name: Oasis
companies.description: Oasis Security is a Non-Human Identity (NHI) management and security platform for hybrid and multi-cloud environments. Its Agentic Access Management (AAM) offering discovers, inventories, governs, and secures service accounts, service principals, managed identities, API keys, secrets, and AI agent credentials across AWS, Azure, GCP, Okta, HashiCorp, Snowflake, GitHub, Salesforce, and AI services such as OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock. The platform provides automated discovery and risk assessment, ownership and context mapping, posture management, threat detection and anomaly monitoring, policy-driven governance and remediation, time-bound provisioning, and secure secret rotation. Founded in New York and backed by Sequoia Capital, Accel, Cyberstarts, and Maple Venture Capital, Oasis extends zero-trust and PAM practices to the fast-growing population of non-human and agentic identities.

companies.name: OpenX
companies.description: OpenX is an independent supply-side platform (SSP) and programmatic ad exchange headquartered in Pasadena, California, founded in 2008. OpenX connects publishers and app developers to advertiser demand through a real-time marketplace that runs OpenRTB-based auctions across display, video, CTV, native, and mobile inventory. Its product suite is organized around the OpenX Exchange (the core marketplace), OpenXSelect (curation, deal creation, and supply-path targeting), OpenXBuild (a software toolkit for assembling custom supply-side workflows and real-time bidstream integrations), and OpenXControl (publisher yield management and demand routing). OpenX exposes several developer-facing APIs documented at docs.openx.com — an OpenRTB API for DSP bidding integrations, a Platform API for account, inventory, demand, targeting, and deal management, a Reporting API for analytics and performance metrics, an OpenXSelect GraphQL API for managing audiences/deals/inventory lists, and an OpenXBuild Real-Time Bidstream API — but the references are gated behind OAuth and OpenX does not publish a public OpenAPI specification or Postman collection. The company is a major contributor to the Prebid.org header-bidding ecosystem (Prebid.js and Prebid Server) and maintains a large GitHub organization with OAuth-based API client libraries in Python, PHP, Java, Perl, and Ruby for the legacy OX3 API. OpenX's business model is transaction-fee based — it takes a share of each ad impression cleared through its exchange — and access to the developer APIs requires an active OpenX account and BD/account-management onboarding rather than self-service signup.

companies.name: Prodigy Education
companies.description: Prodigy Education is a Canadian K-8 game-based learning company best known for Prodigy Math and Prodigy English — fantasy RPG-style products in which students battle and quest by answering curriculum-aligned questions. The product is free for teachers and is monetized through optional parent memberships. Prodigy is consumer- and classroom-facing with no public developer API or partner program. Its integration surface is school rostering and SSO: Clever (SSO + Secure Sync district rostering), ClassLink (SSO, with OneRoster district rostering rolling out), and Google (SSO + Google Classroom assignment creation).

companies.name: Dewu (POIZON)
companies.description: Dewu (POIZON) is a leading Chinese online marketplace for sneakers, streetwear, luxury goods, and collectibles, distinguished by its integrated product authentication (legit-check) service that verifies items before they ship to buyers. Operated by Shanghai-based Poizon and backed by Hongshan (formerly Sequoia China), it runs both the domestic Dewu (得物) app and the global POIZON marketplace. For developers it operates the POIZON / Dewu Open Platform (open.poizon.com and open.dewu.com), a partner program that lets sellers, ISVs, and ERP integrators connect to the marketplace over an app-key plus request-signature authenticated API covering product data, pricing, catalog search, delivery modes, and vendor information.

companies.name: Memorick
companies.description: Memorick is a 500 Global-backed company operating a live web application at memorick.com. Based on its observable application surface, it is a destination photography booking platform connecting customers with photographers across destinations, handling packages, orders, reviews, coupons, and messaging. The product is built on Laravel (Inertia.js single-page front end) and exposes an OAuth2 authorization server via Laravel Passport (authorize/token/clients/scopes plus personal access tokens), Sanctum first-party session auth, and optional two-factor authentication. It publishes no public API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal at this time; the /api/* routes back the first-party application and are authentication-gated. This profile was enriched from live probing of the public surface.

companies.name: TAAI Labs, Inc

Sparkle works across five phases — contextualize, design, build, validate, and govern — and deploys "Secure Agents" that surface risks, gather evidence, and track security decisions to give product security, AppSec, platform engineering, and engineering leadership teams audit-ready visibility across the secure SDLC. The company markets outcomes such as increased security-team productivity, reduced AI-generated risk, and full visibility, and is backed by 500 Global. The product is pre-general-availability and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation as of this profile.

companies.name: Prosimo
companies.description: Prosimo is a multi-cloud networking platform that gives enterprises a full-stack cloud transit, security, performance, observability, and cost-management layer across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle Cloud. Its Application eXperience Infrastructure (AXI) abstracts cloud-provider networking constructs and ties network transit, micro-segmentation, zero-trust policy, WAF, and observability into an autonomous, ML-driven control plane. Prosimo exposes that control plane programmatically through a first-party Terraform provider (prosimo-io/prosimo) for full lifecycle management of cloud gateways, network and application onboarding, policies, namespaces, and security profiles; a companion Pulumi bridge repository and reusable Terraform modules are published on GitHub. Prosimo was venture-backed by General Catalyst, WRVI Capital, and BlackRock; industry sources report it was subsequently acquired by Palo Alto Networks.

companies.name: Theom
companies.description: Theom is a cloud Data & AI Operations Center that governs and secures enterprise data estates, providing automated data security, compliance, and safe generative-AI data activation across multi-cloud environments. Founded in December 2020 by former Cisco, Google, and Yahoo security practitioners (creators of Tetration Analytics), Theom detects active data breaches, maps real-time data lineage, analyzes identity-aware data usage and insider threats, and enforces data-usage policy agentlessly. Its product spans Theom Core (data security and lineage), Theom AI (GenAI leak prevention), and Theom Trust (real-time data contracts). Theom is backed by Wing Venture Capital, Ridge Ventures, Snowflake Ventures, Databricks Ventures, SentinelOne Ventures, and M12, and was named a Leader in the 2026 Forrester Wave for Sensitive Data Discovery and Classification. Theom is delivered as an enterprise platform; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API docs.

companies.name: Zatanna
companies.description: Zatanna is a Y Combinator (W2026) startup based in San Francisco that creates APIs for software that doesn't have any. It reverse-engineers the back ends of web-based cloud and on-prem software — ERPs (SAP), PMS/POS systems, insurance portals, and marketplaces — by observing real workflows, reconstructing the underlying request sequences, and hosting them as clean, callable APIs. Rather than relying on slow browser automation or computer-use agents, Zatanna gives AI agents faster, cheaper, and more reliable integrations, with a reliability layer that handles session management, authentication, and change detection. The agent-facing surface is a hosted, OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at api.zatanna.ai.

companies.name: Feesable
companies.description: Feesable is a fintech infrastructure company providing embedded finance and debt capital management (treasury) tooling that connects platforms, lenders, and capital markets. Its Embedded Finance product delivers white-labeled loan origination infrastructure — KYC/KYB verification, credit decisioning, dynamic pricing, fraud detection, and servicing/collections — exposed through APIs, SDKs, and embeddable widgets so SaaS platforms, marketplaces, and B2B lenders can launch embedded lending without building fintech from scratch. Its Debt Capital Management (DCM Engine) product provides institutional-grade treasury management — credit facility modeling, covenant monitoring, borrowing-base calculations, and automated lender/regulatory reporting connected to live portfolio data. Feesable targets GCC markets with Shariah-compliant options and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. The developer surface (APIs, SDKs, sandbox keys, documentation) is partner-gated behind a partnership onboarding process rather than publicly self-serve.

companies.name: Hidden Level
companies.description: Hidden Level is a U.S.-based defense and aerospace technology company that turns radio-frequency (RF) activity into trusted airspace intelligence. Its passive RF sensing platform detects and tracks unmanned aerial systems (drones) and other activity across air, ground, sea, and space domains without requiring emitters or heavy on-site infrastructure. Hidden Level packages this as hardware sensor platforms, software platforms, and data platforms serving defense and military, critical infrastructure protection, homeland security, and public safety customers. The company hosts its platform on AWS with least-privilege access, MFA, and TLS 1.3 API communications, aligns corporate controls to NIST SP 800-171, and emphasizes U.S. design and manufacturing. Backed by Costanoa Ventures. This API Evangelist profile tracks Hidden Level's public web and security surface; the company does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs.

companies.name: Identiq
companies.description: Identiq operates a privacy-preserving, peer-to-peer identity validation network that lets member companies confirm a customer is already known and trusted by other members without any party sharing, exposing, or centralizing personal data. Its patented anonymized protocol keeps identity data encrypted inside each member's own environment while answering cross-network trust queries in real time. Products include customer identification, sign-up validation, risk-based onboarding, payment optimization, and trust & safety, serving travel, e-commerce, ticketing, fintech, telco, and marketplace verticals. Identiq is a cybersecurity company backed by Insight Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; it publishes a public trust center but no public developer API.

companies.name: Wenspiredata
companies.description: Wenspiredata is an enterprise cybersecurity vendor delivering all-in-one, zero-trust Privileged Remote Access Management (RPAM) for high-risk access. Its platform secures and governs remote privileged access for IT, OT, and third-party vendors, including air-gapped and industrial (OT) environments, and pairs with OsecT for OT-native intrusion detection and continuous visibility. Wenspiredata also offers security assessment services (external attack surface and internal vulnerability assessments) and helps organizations across manufacturing, telecom, finance, and healthcare meet regulatory compliance requirements. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment; the company markets a demo-led enterprise product and does not publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Oligo
companies.description: Oligo Security is a runtime security platform built for the AI era, giving security teams real-time visibility and protection across applications, cloud infrastructure, and AI systems. Oligo combines Cloud Application Detection and Response (CADR), runtime software composition analysis (SCA) and SBOM generation, container scanning, and AI security posture management to detect and stop attacks at the application layer before they spread. By observing which vulnerable code actually executes at runtime, Oligo proves exploitability and reduces vulnerability noise by up to 90-99%, letting teams prioritize the small fraction of findings that are truly reachable. The platform covers apps, workloads, hosts, and cloud infrastructure, and adds runtime protection for AI agents and models. Oligo is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and counts organizations such as Databricks, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Instacart, and Cresta among its customers. Its customer platform and API documentation are gated behind authentication; no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or MCP server is published on the open web at the time of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: SlashNext
companies.description: SlashNext is an AI-native phishing and social-engineering threat detection company founded by Atif Mushtaq (an architect of FireEye's core malware sandbox). Its Real-Time Phishing Threat Intelligence is delivered through the SlashNext On-demand Threat Intelligence (OTI) REST API at oti.slashnext.cloud, which offers URL and host reputation lookups, real-time cloud SEER-engine URL scanning in both asynchronous and blocking modes, and forensic downloads (screenshot, HTML, and rendered text) keyed by scan id, plus per-tenant API quota status. Responses are available as JSON, CSV, or plaintext and every request authenticates with a per-tenant API key passed as the authkey parameter. SlashNext was acquired by Varonis Systems in August 2025 and its detection capabilities are being integrated into the Varonis Email Security and MDDR platform.

companies.name: Grapes
companies.description: Grape (Grape Protocol / GrapeDAO, built by Grape-Labs) is Solana-based decentralized infrastructure that gives online communities and DAOs a set of mainnet-ready primitives for identity, reputation, verification, access control, rewards, and governance. Its products include OG (Vine) Reputation Spaces for season-based on-chain reputation, Grape Verification for identity attestation, the Grape Access Protocol (GPASS) for token/credential-gated access, a GSPL DAO directory, a multi-chain Grape Wallet, and a suite of Discord automation bots. Grape ships no REST/OpenAPI surface; developers integrate through first-party TypeScript SDKs (npm) that wrap its Solana programs directly. Backed by Multicoin Capital, it was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Apiphani
companies.description: Apiphani is a technology-enabled application managed-services company dedicated to helping businesses minimize the effort and risk of running their tier-1, mission-critical applications. It combines decades of enterprise operations experience with intelligent automation and machine learning to drive efficiency and reliability across SAP environments (S/4HANA, Business Suite, Cloud ERP) running on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Services span application technical management (ABAP, SAP Basis, application security), application hosting (ALM/APM), application infrastructure (auto-scaling, HA/DR), security management, and cloud migration and optimization. Apiphani's Luumen platform is an AI-native observability product with "Deep Automation" that detects and resolves issues before users notice, unifying application telemetry, security, and self-healing. The company is certified SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and CSA STAR, and is backed by Insight Partners.

companies.name: Semperis
companies.description: Semperis provides identity-first cybersecurity and disaster recovery for hybrid Active Directory, Entra ID, and Okta environments. Its platform prevents, detects, and responds to identity-based attacks and enables rapid recovery to a trusted state. Products include Directory Services Protector (AD/Entra ID threat prevention, detection, and response), Active Directory Forest Recovery, Disaster Recovery for Entra Tenant, Recovery for Okta, Lightning Intelligence security posture assessment, Delegation Manager, Migrator for AD, and the Ready1 crisis-response platform, alongside the free community tools Purple Knight and Forest Druid. Backed by Insight Partners, Semperis serves enterprises defending the identity attack surface. This profile was enriched from public sources; Semperis publishes no public developer/REST API surface as of this pass.

companies.name: Ziff Davis Enterprise
companies.description: Ziff Davis (Nasdaq: ZD) is a vertically focused digital media and internet company whose portfolio includes leading brands across technology, entertainment, shopping, health, cybersecurity, and marketing technology. Its brands include PCMag, Mashable, IGN, Lifehacker, RetailMeNot, Spiceworks, Everyday Health, IPVanish, Ookla (Speedtest), FullContact, and iContact, among others. The company operates a portfolio of advertising, subscription, and performance-marketing businesses rather than a single first-party public API product. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead; a public web crawl of the corporate site found an active investor-relations, newsroom, brands, privacy, and terms surface but no developer portal, API reference, or published API specification at the corporate (ziffdavis.com) level.

companies.description: Quantifind is a financial crimes automation company founded in 2009 by physicists Ari Tuchman and John Stockton to extract meaningful risk signals from large, unstructured datasets. Graphyte spans watchlist and sanctions screening, adverse media screening, enhanced due diligence, credit risk, and investigations, and is delivered through GraphyteSearch (an investigation application), GraphyteQueue (an AI-native case manager), GraphyteAPI (a synchronous REST risk-assessment API), and GraphyteBatch (batch screening). Quantifind serves Tier 1 and regional banks, digital banks, Fortune 50 companies, and federal and defense agencies, and integrates with case-management systems such as Oracle FCCM. Backed by a16z.

Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, SAIC serves the U.S. federal government with approximately $7.4 billion in annual revenues. The company delivers IT modernization, cloud computing, digital transformation, cybersecurity, AI/ML, and data analytics solutions primarily for defense, intelligence, and civilian government customers. companies.name: Chipper Cash
companies.description: Chipper Cash is a pan-African fintech (legal entities Critical Ideas, Inc. and Voyse Technologies US, Inc.) operating a mobile-first cross-border money transfer, digital payments, crypto, and investing platform across Africa and the diaspora. Founded in 2018 by Ham Serunjogi (Uganda) and Maijid Moujaled (Ghana) after they met at Grinnell College in Iowa, Chipper became one of Africa's fintech unicorns in 2021 and has raised over $340M to date. The consumer app — available on iOS, Android, and web — supports peer-to-peer and cross-border transfers across 21+ African countries, virtual Visa cards (Chipper Card), bill pay and airtime top-ups, fractional US-stock investing (Chipper Stocks, 6,000+ public companies, from $1), and historically crypto trading (BTC/ETH). Reported scale includes 5M+ registered users, 1M+ Visa cards issued, and 250,000+ daily transactions. Direct consumer markets include Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda, Tanzania, South Africa, Rwanda, the UK, and the US. On the developer side, Chipper exposes the Chipper Network API ("Pay With Chipper") — a merchant-facing API that lets authorized businesses accept cross-border payments across 9 currencies, initiate payouts, issue refunds, and look up Chipper user accounts, authenticated with a Chipper User ID + Network API Key. Documentation is published as a Postman collection and access is gated by merchant onboarding; no public OpenAPI or open-source SDK is currently published. Adjacent products include Chipper ID (AI-led identity verification), Chipper Enterprise (bulk payments and collections), Business Accounts, and Zoona (agent-network remittances), plus an integration with TBD's tbDEX protocol for decentralized cross-border payments.

companies.name: Global ID
companies.description: GlobaliD (global.id) is a decentralized digital-identity platform that lets people create a portable, self-sovereign identity and lets developers add "Sign in with GlobaliD" login, issue verifiable credentials, and verify identity claims (such as proof of being 18+) through server-side issuer and verifier toolkits built on Hyperledger Aries. Developers create apps in the invitation-based developer portal to obtain OAuth2 client credentials, then integrate using the official @globalid npm SDKs. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global.
