companies.name: SkySafe
companies.description: SkySafe is a San Diego-based drone-detection and airspace-intelligence company (founded 2015, backed by a16z) whose cloud SaaS platform lets airports, critical infrastructure, law enforcement, universities, correctional facilities, and government customers detect, track, analyze, and act on every drone in their airspace in real time. The platform surfaces precise drone location, altitude, velocity, flight status, launch point, and pilot location, receives and analyzes Remote ID, retains historical flight telemetry for forensic "Prosecutor-Ready" reporting, and pushes instant notifications via SMS, Microsoft Teams, Slack, or CommandCentral Aware. SkySafe advertises integration APIs that push detection, forensics, and analytics into third-party command centers and mitigation workflows, but its developer surface (app.skysafe.io, docs.skysafe.io, api.skysafe.io) sits entirely behind customer authentication — there is no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification to harvest.

companies.name: MDClone
companies.description: MDClone is a healthcare data company whose ADAMS platform gives health systems, life-sciences organizations, and researchers self-service access to explore, analyze, and share clinical data. Its signature capability is a synthetic-data engine that generates non-reversible, artificially created datasets which preserve the statistical characteristics and correlations of real patient data without carrying any protected health information (PHI), removing re-identification risk. The platform lets users organize source data, generate synthetic versions on demand, run analytics, and apply generative AI to accelerate research and improve patient outcomes. MDClone is enterprise/customer-gated: access, support, and any programmatic data-export API are provisioned to licensed customers rather than published as a public developer program.

companies.name: Remind
companies.description: Remind is a K-12 school-home communication platform that lets teachers, schools, and districts message students and families by text, app, email, and voice without exchanging personal phone numbers. The product line includes Remind Chat, a free two-way messaging service used by individual teachers and classrooms, and Remind Hub, a paid district-wide communications platform with administrative controls, SIS integration, delivery analytics, and translation into 90+ languages. Remind reports use in roughly 80% of US public schools and by a majority of US teachers. In November 2023, Santa Barbara-based ParentSquare acquired Remind, and the combined company now operates under the ParentSquare name with Remind Hub continuing for existing district customers and Remind Chat continuing for classroom-level use; Remind Tutoring was discontinued as part of the combination. Remind's only externally documented developer surface is the Share on Remind SDK (the "Remind Share SDK"), a partner program that lets approved third-party content providers embed the Remind composer into their own product, authenticate Remind users via OAuth 2.0, serve shareable content and previews via partner-hosted webhooks, and ship messages back through Remind. companies.name: CODEOWNERS
companies.description: CODEOWNERS is the file format originally introduced by GitHub and later adopted by GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud, Gitea, and Azure Repos that lets a repository declare which individuals or teams are responsible for a path or pattern within the codebase. Platforms use it to auto-request reviews on pull/merge requests, enforce required approvals via branch protection or push rules, and route pings on issues. The file is plain text with one rule per line - a glob pattern followed by one or more owner handles (`@username` or `@org/team`) or email addresses. Comments start with `#` and the last matching pattern wins.

Founded by Joshua Wang and Sanmay Sarada, the platform orchestrates specialized AI agents across the full biometrics lifecycle - standards mapping, data normalization, CDISC mapping, SDTM and ADaM dataset generation, TFLs/TLFs, SAP, eCRFs, Define-XML, QC, and submission documents - turning a protocol and raw study data into FDA-submission-ready output. Astraea is positioned as sponsor-run software rather than a CRO: it runs inside the customer's own secure environment so clinical data never reaches Astraea's servers, with 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and audit-ready, standards-native traceability. The company reports serving 10+ global pharma and biotech sponsors with 30-50% faster reporting cycles.

companies.name: Blackcart
companies.description: Blackcart is a Try Before You Buy (TBYB) platform for ecommerce merchants that lets online shoppers order products, receive them at home, and pay only for what they keep during a trial window. The platform pairs a proprietary fraud and AI order-decisioning engine with storefront integrations for Shopify, Magento, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, WordPress, and custom storefronts, and charges merchants a revenue share on kept items rather than upfront or integration fees. Founded circa 2019 and backed by a 2021 US$8.8M Series A (investors include 500 Global), Blackcart exposed a Beta REST API (order cancellation, refunds, product/store endpoints) documented on Stoplight. As of this enrichment pass its primary domains (blackcart.com and its *.blackcart.com subdomains) return Fastly "unknown domain" errors and blackcart.co serves only a JavaScript redirect shell, indicating the public product and developer surface is offline or the company has wound down.

companies.name: Incandor
companies.description: Incandor is a San Francisco based Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building behavioral intelligence infrastructure for fraud and abuse detection. Rather than relying on identity verification at account creation, Incandor constructs a behavioral map of every user on a platform from how they physically interact with an app or website — mouse dynamics, keystroke timing, scroll patterns, and on mobile how a device is held. It requires no fraud labels and no enrollment period, working from the first session. At the individual level it identifies account takeovers with greater than 99 percent accuracy; at the population level it separates out coordinated fraud rings, mule operators, shared operators, bots and agents, and coerced or duress sessions. Incandor is delivered as a programmable API and a client-side telemetry SDK rather than a black-box risk score, letting fraud teams combine behavioral signals with their own transaction history, customer records, and business rules. It collects only behavioral signals — not what users type, read, or view — keeping user data private by design. The company was founded by Matthew Yekell (CEO) and Luc Rosenzweig (CTO), both Stanford CS graduates. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; the developer platform is currently early access.

companies.name: Fraudio
companies.description: Fraudio is an Amsterdam-based payments fraud detection and financial-crime scale-up founded in 2019 by João Moura (CEO), Nathan Trousdell (COO), and team, with additional offices in London, Lisbon, and Barcelona. Fraudio delivers AI- and machine-learning-driven fraud detection as a managed service to merchant acquirers, payment service providers, card issuers, and banks, with a product line that covers card payment fraud, merchant initiated fraud, anti-money laundering, authorised push payment (APP) fraud, and money mule detection. The company markets itself as "Generation 3" fraud detection, advancing past rule-based (Gen 1) and bespoke per-customer ML (Gen 2) approaches by training a single centralized "patent pending AI super brain" on the pooled transaction history of all of its customers, claiming network-effect performance gains versus single-tenant models. Fraudio integrates with customers through a plug-and-play real-time scoring API with sub-100ms response times, configurable risk-appetite thresholds, and no upfront integration or setup cost. Customers include Viva Wallet, Silverflow, Pismo, Bancontact, Fazz, PayTabs, IXOPAY, Bold.co, SaltPay, WiPay, ePayco, and LOQR. Fraudio is ISO 27001 certified, was selected for the Visa Innovation Program (2023), is co-financed by the EU Lisboa 2030 programme, has raised roughly $3.3M seed plus a Series A round (March 2025), and counts BigStar Ventures, BYND Venture Capital, Teya, Viva Wallet, Portugal Ventures, Iberis Capital, Shilling, and CTT among its investors. There is no public developer portal, no open API reference, no public OpenAPI spec, no SDK, and no GitHub organization — the fraud-scoring API is delivered as a gated B2B integration through a commercial sales process.

Founded in 2026 by Fabian Amherd and John Bachmann and based in San Francisco, Mount aims to rebuild the commercial-insurance carrier stack from the ground up with AI at its core. companies.name: HiddenLayer
companies.description: HiddenLayer is an Austin, Texas-based AI security company founded in March 2022 by Chris Sestito (CEO), Tanner Burns (Chief Scientist), and Jim Ballard (CIO) — former Cylance researchers who encountered a real-world attack on production ML models. HiddenLayer builds an AI Security Platform that protects machine learning and generative AI systems across their entire lifecycle, comprising four integrated modules: AI Discovery (catalogs AI assets and eliminates shadow AI), AI Supply Chain Security (Model Scanner inspects models, weights, and pickle/RDS files for malicious payloads and backdoors), AI Attack Simulation (continuous adversarial red-teaming for agentic and generative systems), and AI Runtime Security / AIDR (a real-time detection-and-response firewall using deterministic classifiers that sit outside the model inference path to detect prompt injection, jailbreaks, indirect attacks, data leakage, and malicious tool calls in agentic and MCP systems). The platform exposes native connectors for CI/CD, MLOps, SIEM/SOAR, API gateways, and major data and cloud platforms, plus guardrail integrations for OpenAI Agents, LangChain, AWS Strands, Microsoft Agent Framework, Azure APIM, and a GitHub Action for Model Scanner. HiddenLayer publishes Python, TypeScript, and Java/Kotlin SDKs and research-grade tooling such as HiddenPickle (Python pickle disassembler/patcher) and HiddenPromise (R .rdx/.rdb/.rds disassembler). The company has raised $56M total ($50M Series A in September 2023 led by M12 / Microsoft's Venture Fund and Moore Strategic Ventures, with Booz Allen Ventures, IBM Ventures, Capital One Ventures, and Ten Eleven Ventures participating) and serves Fortune 500 enterprises, financial services, and US Federal agencies. The HiddenLayer SaaS console and REST API are gated behind enterprise sales and not publicly self-serve, placing this profile in Tier-3 (enterprise-gated) coverage.

companies.name: Customer Database
companies.description: Customer Database is the topic dedicated to APIs, schemas, vocabularies, and reference designs for the systems of record that store customer identity, profile, contact, preference, consent, and account data. companies.name: Customer Portals
companies.description: Customer Portals is the topic dedicated to the architecture, APIs, schemas, and reference designs behind self-service customer portals. A customer portal is a secure web or mobile experience where authenticated customers can manage their profile, view orders and invoices, pay bills, submit and track support tickets, download documents, manage notification preferences, and access account-specific resources. Modern customer portals are typically composed of multiple back-end APIs - authentication and identity, profile and preference management, billing and invoicing, support and ticketing, notifications, and document delivery - surfaced through a single front-end shell. This repository tracks the vendors, patterns, and standards that make customer portals reliable, accessible, and API-driven.

companies.description: Legato Systems, Inc. was a storage management software company founded in 1988 in Palo Alto, California by four former Sun Microsystems engineers — Jon Kepecs, Bob Lyon, Joe Moran, and Russell Sandberg. Its flagship product, NetWorker, was introduced for Unix in 1990 and became one of the defining enterprise backup, recovery, and archiving platforms of the client-server era, centralizing scheduled backup, media management, and disaster recovery across heterogeneous Unix, Windows, and NetWare environments. Backed by Mayfield, the company went public in July 1995. EMC Corporation announced its acquisition of Legato in July 2003 and completed it in October 2003 for an estimated $1.3 billion, folding the product line into EMC's information-management portfolio. NetWorker survives today as Dell EMC NetWorker following Dell's 2016 acquisition of EMC. No Legato-branded developer or API surface remains: the legato.com domain carries Akamai nameservers but publishes no website, and the company predates modern package registries, so no first-party client libraries exist. This profile is retained as a historical Mayfield portfolio record.

Its LightCyber Magna platform shipped as a set of appliances and services (Magna Detector, Magna Probe, Magna Master, Magna Pathfinder, and the Magna Cloud Expert System) and was positioned for user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA), network traffic analysis, security visibility, and PCI compliance. The company was backed by Battery Ventures, Glilot Capital Partners, Amplify Partners, and angel investor Shlomo Kramer. Palo Alto Networks announced the completed acquisition of LightCyber for $105 million in cash on February 28, 2017, and engineered its automated behavioral analytics into the Palo Alto Networks security platform. The independent LightCyber brand, product line, and web presence no longer exist; the lightcyber.com domain has since lapsed from Palo Alto Networks' control and now resolves to an unrelated third-party site. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company lead and carries no live API artifacts.

companies.name: Secure Tunneling Protocols
companies.description: Network protocols that create encrypted tunnels for secure data transmission over untrusted networks, including VPN technologies like IPsec, SSL/TLS, WireGuard, and SSH tunneling for protecting communication channels. It is widely adopted across industries to safeguard digital assets and reduce security risks.

companies.name: Security by Design
companies.description: A software development approach that integrates security considerations and practices from the initial design phase through the entire development lifecycle, rather than adding security as an afterthought. It plays a critical role in protecting organizational assets and maintaining a strong security posture.

companies.name: Security Protocols
companies.description: A set of rules and standards that define how data is transmitted securely over networks, including protocols like SSL/TLS, HTTPS, SSH, and IPsec that provide encryption, authentication, and data integrity. It plays a critical role in protecting organizational assets and maintaining a strong security posture.

companies.name: Security Standards and Procedures

companies.name: Accel
companies.description: Accel is one of the world's leading venture capital firms, founded in 1983 by Arthur Patterson and Jim Swartz and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with additional offices in San Francisco, London, and Bangalore, India. Accel describes itself as "the first partner to exceptional teams everywhere," backing founders from seed and early stage through growth worldwide. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, consumer, artificial intelligence, fintech, cybersecurity, infrastructure and developer tools, security, media, and healthcare, and operates dedicated funds for the US, Europe/Israel, and India/Southeast Asia. Accel is known for its "prepared mind" investment philosophy and for backing category-defining companies including Facebook, Slack, Dropbox, Atlassian, CrowdStrike, UiPath, Qualtrics, Spotify, Flipkart, Swiggy, Freshworks, 1Password, Vercel, Scale AI, Anthropic, and Perplexity. Its portfolio spans more than 100 unicorns, dozens of IPOs, and hundreds of acquisitions. In 2024 Accel raised a $650M fund for European and Israeli startups, and in 2025 raised a fund for India and Southeast Asia. This profile tracks Accel's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Alloy
companies.description: Alloy is a New York-based identity decisioning platform that helps banks, credit unions, and fintechs onboard, monitor, and protect customers across KYC, KYB, AML, fraud, credit, and ongoing-monitoring use cases. The Alloy API exposes the platform's evaluations, journey applications, entities, events, documents, cases, investigations, lists, and webhooks for programmatic identity decisioning and ongoing risk monitoring.

companies.name: Amplify Partners
companies.description: Amplify Partners is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2012 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with a second office in San Francisco. Amplify positions itself as "the first investor for technical founders" — engineers, researchers, and scientists who have felt a problem viscerally and are compelled to spend a decade solving it. The firm invests primarily at the seed and Series A stages, with check sizes generally ranging from roughly $1M to $10M (often around $3M at seed), and continues to back companies through growth and IPO. Its thesis concentrates on deep technical categories: developer tools and computing infrastructure, machine learning and artificial intelligence, data and analytics, cybersecurity, and digital biology. In June 2025 Amplify announced roughly $900M in new capital across three vehicles — Fund 6, Fund 6 Select, and Amplify Bio. Notable portfolio companies include Datadog, Fastly, dbt Labs, Temporal, Chainguard, LangChain, Runway, and Recursion.

companies.name: Apstal
companies.description: AI-first website analytics and visitor tracking platform that replaces traditional dashboards with a natural-language chatbot interface, offering conversational analytics, cookieless tracking, session replays, and heatmaps. Programmatic access is provided through a hosted MCP server exposing analytics tools.

companies.name: Arthur Ventures
companies.description: Arthur Ventures is a Minneapolis, Minnesota venture capital firm that invests in early-stage B2B software companies with a global reach. The firm backs capital-efficient, founder-led software businesses across the United States and internationally, partnering with teams building enterprise and vertical SaaS, cybersecurity, developer tools, and data infrastructure. Arthur Ventures manages approximately $2B in assets under management, including roughly $800M in current active funds, and supports a portfolio of 60+ active companies. Notable portfolio investments include ThreatLocker, DNSFilter, Nucleus Security, DataCamp, Total Expert, Recast Software, CertifID, Hudu, Stream, and Macabacus. The firm is led by general partners Patrick Meenan, Ryan Kruizenga, and Andrew Heim, with offices at 250 Nicollet Mall in downtown Minneapolis.

companies.name: Bain Capital Ventures
companies.description: Bain Capital Ventures (BCV) is the venture capital arm of Bain Capital, a multi-stage, domain-focused venture business founded in 2001 with roughly $9.4B in assets under management (as of June 30, 2025). BCV incubates ideas, leads seed rounds, and scales growth-stage companies, investing from about $1M of seed capital through $100M of growth equity and partnering with more than 400 active portfolio companies. The firm concentrates on AI Apps, AI Infrastructure, Commerce, Fintech, Healthcare, Physical AI, and Security, backing companies such as MaintainX (acquired by Autodesk), Moveworks (acquired by ServiceNow), Redis, Crusoe, Cognition, Decagon, Legora, and Sunday Robotics. BCV operates from New York City, Palo Alto, and San Francisco, and pairs its investments with a "partnerships over playbooks" platform (The Hive) supporting talent, go-to-market, and customer development.

companies.name: Bessemer Venture Partners
companies.description: Bessemer Venture Partners (BVP) is one of the oldest and largest venture capital firms in the world, founded in 1911 out of the fortune of steel magnate Henry Phipps and headquartered in San Francisco, California. With more than $20 billion in assets under management and investment teams in San Francisco, Silicon Valley, New York, Boston, London, Bangalore, and Tel Aviv, Bessemer invests globally across seed, early, and growth stages, and runs a dedicated private equity buyout arm, BVP Forge. The firm invests across artificial intelligence and machine learning, cloud and infrastructure, developer tools, cybersecurity, fintech, healthcare and biotech, consumer, marketplaces, vertical software, data, deep tech and defense, and crypto/web3. Bessemer has backed transformative companies including Shopify, Twilio, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Yelp, DocuSign, Wix, Fiverr, Toast, ServiceTitan, PagerDuty, Auth0, Box, and Canva, and is known for publishing its "Anti- Portfolio" of missed opportunities, its Atlas research roadmaps, and its cloud/state-of-the-industry benchmark reports. Investing out of its 12th early-stage fund (a $3.85B vehicle), Bessemer was ranked among the largest venture firms by five-year fundraising. This profile tracks Bessemer's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Certificate Enrolment Protocols
companies.description: Certificate Enrolment Protocols are the interoperable standards that automate the lifecycle operations of requesting, issuing, renewing, and revoking X.509 digital certificates between Certificate Authorities (CAs), Registration Authorities (RAs), and end entities. The four major protocols in active deployment are ACME (RFC 8555, widely adopted via Let's Encrypt and cert-manager for web PKI), SCEP (legacy Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol widely supported in network devices and MDM), EST (RFC 7030, Enrollment over Secure Transport for modern HTTPS-capable devices), and CMP (RFC 4210 / RFC 9480, Certificate Management Protocol for enterprise PKI and industrial automation). This index tracks the specifications, reference implementations, and supporting infrastructure for each.

companies.name: Coadjute
companies.description: Coadjute Ltd is a London-based property technology company that operates a shared network for the UK residential property market, connecting estate agents, conveyancers, mortgage brokers, lenders and consumers through the CRM and case-management systems they already use rather than through any multiple listing service — the UK has no MLS and no RESO adoption. Built on R3 Corda distributed ledger technology and now positioned as a fully managed AML and compliance platform for UK property, Coadjute sits in the middle of the transaction as connective infrastructure: property packs, material information, shareable AML checks and status data moving between parties. Its API posture is partner-only and not publicly reachable. Coadjute's own Partner Terms of Service govern "the Coadjute Applet, APIs, Connector, Sandbox, DLT Application" under an Order Form and Subscription Term, and its Network Acceptable Use Policy names a "Partner Cloud API" and an "End User App Plugin" — but the developer portal that once published an API catalogue at developer.coadjute.com returns HTTP 502 as of 2026-07-26, api.coadjute.com answers only with authenticated JSON error envelopes, and no OpenAPI, Postman collection, SDK or public reference could be retrieved. The only publicly fetchable machine-readable contract is the Auth0-backed OpenID Connect discovery document at auth.coadjute.com. Coadjute publishes no open data; the open property-data layer in its home market belongs to HM Land Registry and Ordnance Survey, not to Coadjute.

companies.name: Costanoa Ventures
companies.description: Costanoa Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in June 2012 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with an additional office in San Francisco. Costanoa invests primarily at the Seed and Series A stages, writing checks of roughly $1M to $10M and taking concentrated 10-15% ownership across about 35 companies per fund. The firm's thesis is to fill the "missing middle" of early-stage venture by providing unusually hands-on, operator-led support to founders building applied AI, AI and data infrastructure, cybersecurity, national security / defense tech, fintech, and enterprise software companies. Costanoa was founded by Greg Sands (an early Netscape product manager) and manages roughly $2.8B in assets. In September 2024 it closed an oversubscribed Fund V at $275M alongside Opportunity Fund III at $119M, doubling down on AI-enabled B2B technology. Portfolio companies include Alation, Cyberhaven, Quizlet, PayNearMe, Auterion, Vannevar Labs, Kepler Communications, and Muon Space.

companies.name: Cowboy Ventures
companies.description: Cowboy Ventures is a seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2012 by Aileen Lee (who coined the term "unicorn" for billion-dollar startups) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The firm backs pre-seed and seed-stage founders building "life-changing" products for large and growing markets, with roughly 70% of investments made pre-product and a strong seed-to-Series A graduation rate. Typical first checks run from about $100K up to $1M, with a sweet spot near $500K–$800K. Cowboy invests across enterprise software, fintech, software infrastructure and security, healthcare, consumer, future of work, and vertical software, primarily in the United States. The firm has made 100+ early-stage investments and cultivates a curated community of founders, operators, and tech leaders. Notable portfolio companies include Chime, Guild, Drata, Dollar Shave Club, Ironclad, Aura, Kiavi, Crunchbase, and Product Hunt.

companies.name: CRV
companies.description: CRV (formerly Charles River Ventures) is one of the oldest venture capital firms in the United States, founded in 1970 to commercialize research coming out of MIT. The firm invests early — primarily at the Seed and Series A stages, with occasional Series B — leading rounds in enterprise, consumer, developer tools, security, data infrastructure, AI, and bioengineering companies. CRV has backed more than 750 companies since inception across 18 funds, raising over $4.3 billion (including a recent $600M early-stage fund), and has seen 80-plus of its portfolio companies reach public-company status. Notable investments include DoorDash, Airtable, HubSpot, Datadog, Zendesk, Patreon, Mercury, Vercel, Cursor, Postman, Kong, Tailscale, Ring, and PillPack. The firm is headquartered in San Francisco (52 Zoe Street) with a long-standing Bay Area presence and offices in Menlo Park, CA and Cambridge, MA.

companies.name: Cybersecurity Standards
companies.description: Cybersecurity Standards captures the public, machine-readable, and reference frameworks that establish best practices for protecting information systems, networks, software, and data from cyber threats. The landscape is anchored by U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) publications such as the Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0, SP 800-53 controls, SP 800-171 controls for controlled unclassified information, the Risk Management Framework (RMF), and the Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF SP 800-218); the international ISO/IEC 27001 / 27002 information security management standard family; the Center for Internet Security (CIS) Critical Security Controls and Benchmarks; the OWASP Top 10 and ASVS for application security; PCI DSS for payment data; HITRUST CSF for healthcare; SOC 2 trust services criteria; and FedRAMP / StateRAMP for cloud authorization. This index aggregates authoritative URLs, machine-readable artifacts (e.g., OSCAL), and cross-references for organizations building or auditing cybersecurity programs.

companies.name: Data Privacy Standards
companies.description: Data Privacy Standards is the landscape of laws, regulations, frameworks, and technical standards that govern the collection, processing, sharing, and protection of personal data. It spans GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, LGPD, PIPEDA, PIPL, HIPAA, ISO/IEC 27701, NIST Privacy Framework, OECD Privacy Principles, and emerging machine-readable consent and preference signals such as IAB TCF, GPC, and W3C DPV.

companies.name: Defense in Depth
companies.description: Defense in Depth is a layered cybersecurity strategy that uses multiple, overlapping security controls so that if one control fails, others continue to protect systems, data, and users. The approach spans physical, network, endpoint, application, identity, and data layers, and is widely referenced in NIST, CISA, NSA, and DoD security guidance. This topic indexes APIs and resources that help organizations design, implement, and verify defense in depth controls.

companies.name: Disclosure Requirements
companies.description: Disclosure Requirements are the regulatory and legal obligations for organizations to reveal specific information to stakeholders, regulators, and the public. These requirements span financial disclosures (SEC, IFRS), sustainability and ESG reporting (CSRD, ESRS, IFRS S1/S2, TCFD, GRI, SASB), privacy notices (GDPR, CCPA), and corporate governance, helping ensure transparency and accountability across markets and jurisdictions.

companies.name: Felicis Ventures
companies.description: Felicis Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2006 by Aydin Senkut and headquartered in Menlo Park, California. The firm backs founders "who rewrite the rules," concentrating the majority of its capital at Seed and Series A while also participating in Series B and select growth rounds, with reported assets under management of roughly $2.4B and a tenth flagship fund (FV X) of $900M closed in June 2025. Typical checks range from about $2M to $40M. Felicis is thesis-driven across artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and defense, global resilience and energy, health and bio, infrastructure, and vertical SaaS, and invests globally (backing founders from 40+ countries rather than only Silicon Valley). The firm leads or co-leads a large share of its deals, sources most new investments through founder referrals, and is known for founder-friendly practices including a commitment to vote with founders on board matters and a "1% Founder Development Pledge." Its portfolio and exits include Shopify, Adyen, Canva, Notion, Credit Karma, Fitbit, Guardant Health, Docker, PagerDuty, Twitch, Supabase, and Runway.

companies.name: GGV Capital
companies.description: GGV Capital (Granite Global Ventures) was a global, multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 2000 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with offices in San Francisco, Shanghai, Beijing, and Singapore. GGV invested from seed through growth stage across Social/Internet and consumer, Enterprise Tech and SaaS, and Smart Tech (fintech, infrastructure, developer tools, cybersecurity, AI, and cross-border commerce), with a distinctive US–Asia bridge thesis. At its peak the firm managed roughly $9.2B in assets under management and backed more than 400 companies, including 44 unicorns and dozens of IPOs — among them Airbnb, Slack, Square, Affirm, HashiCorp, Coinbase, Peloton, Opendoor, Poshmark, StockX, BigCommerce, Grab, Alibaba, ByteDance, Zendesk, and Xpeng. On March 29, 2024 GGV Capital ceased using the GGV brand and split into two independent successor firms amid US–China tensions: Notable Capital (US/international, led by Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon, ~$4.2B AUM) and Granite Asia (Asia, led by Jenny Lee and Jixun Foo, ~$5B AUM). The former ggvc.com companies surface now redirects to Notable Capital, which carries the US/international portfolio graph. This profile tracks GGV Capital's identity and portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: ICONIQ Capital
companies.description: ICONIQ Capital is a global investment firm founded in December 2011 by Divesh Makan, Michael Anders, and Chad Boeding, headquartered in San Francisco, California with offices in Palo Alto, New York, London, and Singapore. ICONIQ operates as a hybrid family office and multi-strategy investment firm serving ultra-high-net-worth technology entrepreneurs, executives, and their families, and reports over $100B in assets under management across investment management, real assets, venture and growth, and impact strategies. Its venture arm, ICONIQ Growth, partners with founders from inception through IPO and beyond, backing category-leading technology companies across enterprise software, infrastructure, data, developer tools, fintech, security, healthcare IT, and — since 2023 — artificial intelligence as a core theme. ICONIQ Growth has invested in 140+ companies and produced notable outcomes including Snowflake, Airbnb, GitLab, HashiCorp, Datadog, Docusign, Adyen, Uber, Zoom, and Procore, alongside active AI positions in Anthropic, OpenAI, Writer, Glean, ElevenLabs, and Sierra.

companies.name: imgauth — API di attestazione opere digitali
companies.description: Digital-work attestation and proof-of-existence service by Spazio Genesi ETS. Clients compute a SHA-256 fingerprint locally (file bytes never leave the device) and receive a signed PDF certificate, an RFC 3161 timestamp, and an OpenTimestamps/Bitcoin anchor. Exposes a public REST API (OpenAPI 3.0.3) and a hosted remote MCP server for agents.

companies.name: Insight Partners
companies.description: Insight Partners is a global software-focused venture capital and private equity firm founded in 1995 by Jeff Horing and Jerry Murdock and headquartered in New York City, with additional offices in London, Tel Aviv, and Palo Alto. The firm invests in high-growth technology and software ScaleUp companies at every stage from early (Series A) through growth and late-stage pre-IPO, deploying checks that range from roughly $5M up to $500M+ and pairing capital with a dedicated in-house operations team (Insight Onsite) that provides talent, sales, marketing, and product expertise to accelerate scaling. Sector emphasis spans enterprise software broadly, including cybersecurity, fintech, AI/ML, DevOps, data infrastructure, and healthtech. With approximately $90B in regulatory assets under management as of 2025 and more than 875 companies backed worldwide, Insight is one of the largest technology investors in the world, with a portfolio and exit history that includes Twitter, Shopify, DocuSign, Wix, SentinelOne, HelloFresh, N26, Alteryx, and AppDynamics.

companies.name: Institutional Venture Partners
companies.description: Institutional Venture Partners (IVP) is a later-stage venture capital and growth equity firm founded in 1980 by Reid Dennis and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with offices in San Francisco and London. One of the oldest venture firms in Silicon Valley, IVP concentrates on the fastest-growing, most prominent late-stage and growth-stage technology companies each year, typically writing checks in the $10M to $100M range and taking a long-term view toward value creation. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, fintech, cybersecurity, developer tools and cloud infrastructure, data and AI, consumer internet, media, gaming, and healthcare. Across roughly 45 years and 18 funds (Fund XVIII closed at $1.6B in 2024) IVP has backed more than 400 companies and seen 135+ IPOs, with roughly $7B–$8B in assets under management. Notable investments and exits include Netflix, Twitter, Snap, Coinbase, Dropbox, GitHub, Slack, Datadog, CrowdStrike, HashiCorp, UiPath, Robinhood, Klarna, Wise, Figma, Grammarly, Rubrik, Discord, Anthropic, Perplexity, and DeepL.

companies.name: Kerberos
companies.description: Kerberos is a computer-network authentication protocol that works on the basis of tickets to allow nodes communicating over a non-secure network to prove their identity to one another in a secure manner. It is widely used in enterprise environments for single sign-on authentication.

companies.name: Lightspeed Venture Partners
companies.description: Lightspeed Venture Partners is a global, multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 2000 by Barry Eggers, Christopher Schaepe, Ravi Mhatre, and Peter Nieh, and headquartered in Menlo Park, California. Lightspeed invests from seed through Series F and beyond, backing bold builders across artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, cloud and enterprise infrastructure, developer tools, fintech, consumer, gaming, and healthcare/biotech. The firm operates as a single global team across roughly a dozen offices in the United States, Europe, Israel, India, and Southeast Asia, with U.S./Europe/Israel run by Lightspeed Management Company (LSVP) and India/Southeast Asia by Lightspeed India Partners (LSIP). Lightspeed reports managing on the order of $25B+ (up to $40B+ by some self-reported figures) across the Lightspeed platform. Notable investments and exits include Anthropic, Mistral AI, ElevenLabs, Wiz, Rubrik, Cato Networks, Stripe, Affirm, Snap, Nutanix, MuleSoft, AppDynamics, Nest, Grafana, ngrok, Faire, and Navan.

companies.name: Menlo Ventures
companies.description: Menlo Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1976 and headquartered in Menlo Park and San Francisco, California, that invests in transformative technology companies across the full early lifecycle. Its strategy spans "the Three Stages of Early" — Inception (validating early ideas, including via the Inception Fund and the Anthology Fund AI accelerator built with Anthropic), Venture (Series A/B), and Inflection (early growth). Menlo invests across artificial intelligence, bio and healthcare, consumer, cybersecurity, defense, fintech, infrastructure, robotics and hardware, SaaS, and supply chain and automation, primarily in North America. Over roughly five decades the firm reports backing companies that produced 85+ public companies and 170+ mergers and acquisitions, with a portfolio that includes Anthropic, Uber, Roku, Chime, Carta, Benchling, Pinecone, Netlify, and Warby Parker. In 2026 Menlo announced $3 billion in fresh capital, the largest raise in the firm's history, and reports $7.6B+ in assets under management. Its ethos is "when we invest, we're invested" — active, hands-on support beyond capital.

companies.name: OAuth
companies.description: OAuth is an open authorization framework that enables third-party applications to access user resources without exposing credentials. It provides a secure, token-based delegation mechanism widely used across the web for granting limited access to APIs and services on behalf of users.

companies.name: ProofDraw
companies.description: Provably-fair random selection REST API that seals entry lists with SHA-256 commitments bound to future drand (League of Entropy) randomness rounds, producing publicly verifiable draw receipts with client-side open-source verification.

companies.name: Redpoint Ventures
companies.description: Redpoint Ventures is a Silicon Valley venture capital firm founded in 1999 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with additional offices in San Francisco and Los Angeles and a history of China-focused funds in Beijing and Shanghai. Redpoint is a multi-stage investor that backs founders from seed and early stage through growth, running dedicated early-stage and growth teams. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, AI and AI infrastructure, cloud and data infrastructure, developer tools, cybersecurity, fintech, consumer internet, healthcare, crypto/web3, and marketplaces. Typical checks range from roughly $0.5M-$2M at seed and $2M-$8M at Series A up to $10M+ at growth stage. As of 2025 Redpoint managed about $4.5 billion in assets, and its partners have participated in 130+ IPOs and acquisitions including Netflix, Snowflake, Twilio, Pure Storage, Zendesk, Stripe, HashiCorp, and HomeAway. The firm launched its tenth flagship fund, a $650M vehicle, in 2025, and publishes the annual InfraRed report on the leading private cloud and infrastructure companies. This profile tracks Redpoint's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Sapphire Ventures
companies.description: Sapphire Ventures is a global software venture capital firm that partners with expansion-stage enterprise technology companies it believes can become category leaders. Originally founded in 1996 as the venture arm of SAP, the firm spun out as an independent company in 2011 and rebranded to Sapphire Ventures in 2014. Sapphire manages over $10 billion in assets under management and typically invests Series B through IPO, with check sizes commonly ranging from roughly $2M to $30M, while its Sapphire Sport and Sapphire Partners arms address early-stage sports/media and fund investing respectively. The firm concentrates on Enterprise AI and B2B software, including data and analytics, cybersecurity, DevOps and developer tools, fintech, health tech, and vertical SaaS. Headquartered in Austin, Texas, with offices in San Francisco, Menlo Park, New York, and London, Sapphire backs companies of consequence and supports them with a large platform team that drives executive talent and customer introductions. The portfolio spans 30+ IPOs and 80+ exits including DocuSign, Square, Wise, monday.com, JFrog, Auth0, MuleSoft, and LinkedIn.

companies.name: Scale Venture Partners
companies.description: Scale Venture Partners (ScaleVP) is an early-stage venture capital firm based in Foster City, California, that invests primarily at Series A and Series B in founders applying AI to how businesses actually work. The firm traces its origins to 2000 as BA Venture Partners, the venture arm of Bank of America, and became an independent partnership in 2007. Scale focuses on AI and B2B software spanning applications, developer tools and infrastructure, and security, and leads roughly 80% of the rounds it joins. Initial checks typically range from $5M to $50M, sized to the round, and the firm looks for signed customers and repeatable demand (commonly $500K–$5M ARR) rather than a fixed revenue bar. Scale reports about $2.8B in assets under management and is currently deploying its $900M Fund VIII, raised in 2022. It invests across North America, Europe, and Israel, and pairs capital with a Go-To-Market advisory bench of CROs, CMOs, and CFOs. Scale has produced 11 IPOs — among the highest rates for early-stage firms — with notable investments including DocuSign, Box, HubSpot, BILL, and JFrog.

companies.name: Shasta Ventures
companies.description: Shasta Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2004 and based in Silicon Valley (Portola Valley / Menlo Park, on and around Sand Hill Road, California). Founded by Rob Coneybeer and Ravi Mohan (with Tod Francis and Jason Pressman among its long-tenured Managing Directors), the firm invests primarily at the Series A stage in United States technology startups, typically leading rounds and taking board seats. Shasta has roughly $1.3B under management across multiple funds (Fund II $250M, Fund III $265M, Fund IV $300M) and a 20-year track record. Its thesis centers on enterprise software / SaaS, cybersecurity, developer tools and infrastructure, data intelligence, camera / computer vision, and consumer subscription products, pairing capital with operational support (Shasta Elevate) for technical founders. Notable investments include Anaplan, Zuora, Nest, Nextdoor, Apptio, Eero, Sendbird, Tonal, Lattice, Highspot, SentinelOne and Turo, with 12 unicorns, multiple IPOs and dozens of acquisitions across its history.

companies.name: True Ventures
companies.description: True Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2006 by Jon Callaghan and Phil Black and headquartered in Palo Alto / San Francisco, California. Operating under a "first to believe" thesis, True writes the initial institutional check and stays invested through every subsequent stage of a company's journey, concentrating on pre-seed, seed, and Series A rounds with check sizes reported in the roughly $500K-$15M range. The firm invests broadly across technology and founder-led categories including software and developer infrastructure, consumer products and internet, healthcare and life sciences, hardware and robotics, climate and energy, security, and AI. With more than $3.8B in committed capital, True has backed 1,050+ founders across 500+ companies since inception, with notable early checks into Fitbit, Peloton, Ring, Automattic/WordPress, HashiCorp, Duo Security, Sweetgreen, Bluesky, and Splice. True is known for its founder-first platform, the True University founder camps, and long-term conviction-led early ownership.

companies.name: Zero Trust
companies.description: Zero Trust is the umbrella cybersecurity strategy that eliminates implicit trust based on network location and requires continuous verification of every user, device, workload, and access request. This index aggregates the core specifications (NIST, CISA, DoD, NSA, NCSC), the leading vendor platforms that implement Zero Trust (Cloudflare, Zscaler, Netskope, Palo Alto Networks, Tailscale, Twingate, Microsoft, Google), and the CNCF-graduated open standards that the ecosystem depends on (SPIFFE, SPIRE, OPA). Three sister API Evangelist topics cover Zero Trust Architecture, Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA), and the Zero Trust Security Model in greater depth.
